EXT-DAPP-WALLET-API.name: DApp via Wallet JSON-RPC API
EXT-DAPP-WALLET-API.rationale: DApps connect to wallets via JSON-RPC provider interface. No authentication beyond basic connection authorization. DApps can submit arbitrary call batches, query capabilities for fingerprinting, and provide malformed parameters. All input must be fully validated.

EXT-DAPP-EVENT-LISTENER.name: DApp Event Listener via Provider Events
EXT-DAPP-EVENT-LISTENER.entry_point: Provider event subscription (tx_speedup, tx_cancel, tx_replacement events per EIP-2831)
EXT-DAPP-EVENT-LISTENER.rationale: DApps listening for transaction replacement events are untrusted consumers. The provider must not leak cross-application information through events. Event data must be scoped to the requesting application.

EXT-FINGERPRINTING-ATTACKER.name: Fingerprinting Attacker via Capability Query
EXT-FINGERPRINTING-ATTACKER.rationale: Malicious actors can use capability queries to fingerprint wallet types and identify targets. Wallet must filter sensitive capabilities for untrusted callers to prevent identification.

EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER-MODEXP.name: Contract Caller via MODEXP Precompile
EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER-MODEXP.rationale: Any contract or EOA can call the MODEXP precompile with arbitrary input data. Inputs include length fields, base, exponent, and modulus which are all attacker-controlled. EIP-7823 bounds (1024 bytes) must be enforced. Gas pricing must accurately reflect computation cost. Zero-padding for short inputs must be handled correctly.

EXT-MODEXP-ATTACKER.name: Attacker via Oversized MODEXP Input
EXT-MODEXP-ATTACKER.entry_point: CALL to address 0x05 with length fields > 1024 bytes
EXT-MODEXP-ATTACKER.rationale: Attacker deliberately submits inputs exceeding EIP-7823 bounds to exploit potential consensus bugs or resource exhaustion. The precompile must reject and consume all gas.

EXT-MESSAGE-CALLER-EVM.name: Message Caller via EVM Interpreter
EXT-MESSAGE-CALLER-EVM.entry_point: EVM message call (CREATE, CALL, DELEGATECALL, etc.)
EXT-MESSAGE-CALLER-EVM.rationale: Any entity can initiate EVM message calls with arbitrary code and data. Stack depth limits (1024), gas accounting, code size limits (24576 bytes), and 0xEF prefix rejection must be enforced. Recursive calls and gas exhaustion are primary attack vectors.

EXT-PEER-NODE-BLOCKS.name: Network Peer via P2P Block Propagation
EXT-PEER-NODE-BLOCKS.entry_point: P2P devp2p block propagation (fork-dependent validation rules, EIP-2070 Berlin)
EXT-PEER-NODE-BLOCKS.rationale: Peer nodes broadcasting blocks are unauthenticated. Blocks must be validated against the correct rule set (pre/post fork). Incorrect fork detection could accept invalid blocks.

EXT-WHISPER-PEER.name: Whisper Network Peer via DEVp2p
EXT-WHISPER-PEER.entry_point: Whisper protocol messages (status 0x00, envelopes 0x01, PoW update 0x02, bloom update 0x03)
EXT-WHISPER-PEER.rationale: Whisper peers are unauthenticated P2P participants. They can send malformed envelopes, invalid PoW values (NaN, INF, negative), flood with low-quality messages, or attempt traffic analysis through bloom filter correlation. All envelopes must be validated for structure, PoW, and topic matching.

EXT-WHISPER-APPLICATION.name: Whisper Application via Local API
EXT-WHISPER-APPLICATION.rationale: Local applications submitting messages through Whisper are semi-trusted (authenticated local access) but message content and encryption parameters must still be validated.

EXT-CL-VALIDATOR-BLOB.name: Validator via Beacon Block Proposal (Fulu)
EXT-CL-VALIDATOR-BLOB.entry_point: Beacon block proposal with blob commitments
EXT-CL-VALIDATOR-BLOB.rationale: Validators proposing blocks with blob KZG commitments are untrusted. The CL must validate that blob commitment count does not exceed the epoch-specific limit from BLOB_SCHEDULE (15 at epoch 412672, 21 at epoch 419072). Incorrect blob count enforcement could cause chain splits.

EXT-BUILDER-VIA-P2P.name: Staked Builder via P2P Network
EXT-BUILDER-VIA-P2P.entry_point: P2P gossip (signed execution payload headers and envelopes)
EXT-BUILDER-VIA-P2P.rationale: Builders submit bids and reveal payloads over the P2P network. Despite being staked, builder equivocation has no slashing penalty, so payload content and timing are untrusted.

EXT-PTC-MEMBER-VIA-P2P.name: PTC Member via P2P Network
EXT-PTC-MEMBER-VIA-P2P.rationale: PTC members are validators attesting to payload timeliness via P2P. Individual attestations are untrusted; only aggregate threshold (256/512) provides confidence.

EXT-COLLUDING-PROPOSERS.name: Colluding Proposer Set via P2P
EXT-COLLUDING-PROPOSERS.entry_point: P2P gossip (beacon blocks for consecutive slots)
EXT-COLLUDING-PROPOSERS.rationale: Proposers controlling consecutive slots with >20% stake can attempt payload reorgs. Fully adversarial model.

EXT-DEPLOYER-VIA-TX.name: Contract Deployer via Transaction
EXT-DEPLOYER-VIA-TX.rationale: Any EOA or contract can initiate contract creation. No authentication beyond valid transaction signature. Deployer may be malicious, attempting address collision attacks.

EXT-CALLING-CONTRACT-VIA-EVM.name: Smart Contract via EVM Call
EXT-CALLING-CONTRACT-VIA-EVM.entry_point: EVM CALL to beacon roots contract (0x000F3df6D732807Ef1319fB7B8bB8522d0Beac02) and ecrecover precompile (0x01)
EXT-CALLING-CONTRACT-VIA-EVM.rationale: Any contract can call the beacon roots contract or ecrecover precompile. Input data is completely untrusted and must be fully validated.

EXT-WALLET-CLIENT-VIA-RPC.name: Wallet/DApp Client via JSON-RPC
EXT-WALLET-CLIENT-VIA-RPC.rationale: Wallet clients query node via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. The response itself is informational and can be spoofed by a malicious node.

EXT-RPC-NODE.name: JSON-RPC Node Operator
EXT-RPC-NODE.rationale: Node operators control the eth_symbol response. A malicious node can return false symbol data to deceive users about network identity. No on-chain verification possible.

EXT-DAPP-VIA-WALLET-API.name: DApp via Wallet Silent Signing API
EXT-DAPP-VIA-WALLET-API.rationale: DApps request silent signing permissions from wallets. Fully untrusted - may be malicious or compromised. Permission scope and secret validation are the only controls.

EXT-DEPOSITOR-VIA-DEPOSIT-CONTRACT.name: Validator Depositor via Deposit Contract
EXT-DEPOSITOR-VIA-DEPOSIT-CONTRACT.rationale: Anyone can deposit 32 ETH to queue a new validator. Deposit data (pubkey, withdrawal credentials) is untrusted input that must be validated.

EXT-PEER-NODE-VIA-P2P.name: Peer Node via P2P Network
EXT-PEER-NODE-VIA-P2P.entry_point: P2P devp2p / etha subprotocol (block propagation, data retrieval, handshake)
EXT-PEER-NODE-VIA-P2P.rationale: Peer nodes propagate blocks and historical data over unauthenticated P2P network. May send oversized blocks, false availability bitmasks, or invalid data. All received data must be fully validated.

EXT-TX-SENDER-VIA-RPC.name: Transaction Sender via JSON-RPC or P2P
EXT-TX-SENDER-VIA-RPC.rationale: Transaction senders submit transactions with arbitrary gas limits and deployment targets. Gas cap (16,777,216) and contract creation collision/storage checks are required validation.

EXT-UNTRUSTED-DATA-SOURCE.name: Untrusted Data Source via Network
EXT-UNTRUSTED-DATA-SOURCE.rationale: Any data from network peers or user transactions is untrusted input that passes through keccak hash functions for integrity verification. Hash function security is foundational.

EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER-VIA-P2P.name: Block Producer via P2P Network
EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER-VIA-P2P.entry_point: P2P block propagation (block headers with PoW/environmental data)
EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER-VIA-P2P.rationale: Block producers set block environmental data (coinbase, timestamp, PREVRANDAO) and submit PoW solutions. Timestamp manipulation within protocol bounds is possible. All block data requires full validation.

EXT-CONTRACT-CREATOR-VIA-EVM.name: Contract Creator via CREATE/CREATE2
EXT-CONTRACT-CREATOR-VIA-EVM.rationale: Any contract or EOA can attempt contract creation. EIP-7610 adds storage emptiness check to EIP-684's nonce/code checks. Must validate target address has zero nonce, zero code, AND empty storage.

EXT-MALICIOUS-PEER-VIA-P2P.name: Malicious Peer via P2P Network
EXT-MALICIOUS-PEER-VIA-P2P.entry_point: P2P devp2p (oversized blocks, false handshake data)
EXT-MALICIOUS-PEER-VIA-P2P.rationale: Attacker nodes may craft blocks exceeding MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8 MiB) or transactions exceeding gas cap to cause resource exhaustion. Early size validation is critical.

EXT-USER-RPC-DEBUG.name: User via Debug/Trace RPC
EXT-USER-RPC-DEBUG.rationale: Trace and simulation requests can trigger expensive computation. Even though debug endpoints may be access-controlled, the data content is untrusted. Maps to EXT-TRACE-REQUESTER, EXT-RPC-CLIENT from source files.

EXT-NETWORK-PEER-EL.name: Network Peer via P2P (EL)
EXT-NETWORK-PEER-EL.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. They may propagate blocks containing invalid transactions (e.g., from contract addresses violating EIP-3607) or blocks with manipulated difficulty/timestamp values. Maps to EXT-NETWORK-PEER from EIP-3607.

EXT-NETWORK-PEER-CL.name: P2P Network Peer via CL Gossip/Req-Resp
EXT-NETWORK-PEER-CL.entry_point: libp2p gossipsub and req/resp (beacon blocks, light client updates)
EXT-NETWORK-PEER-CL.rationale: Network peers deliver blocks to fork choice store (on_block handler) and light client protocol messages. Blocks must pass parent existence, slot timing, finalized descendant, and state transition checks. Light client messages require fork-version-aware SSZ deserialization validation.

EXT-MINING-CLIENT.name: Mining Client via Stratum
EXT-MINING-CLIENT.entry_point: EthereumStratum/2.0.0 TCP Protocol (mining.hello, mining.subscribe, mining.authorize, mining.submit)
EXT-MINING-CLIENT.rationale: Mining clients connect over TCP with session-based authentication (worker tokens). However, the channel is not encrypted by default and message content (solutions, session IDs) must be fully validated. Maps to EXT-MINER from EIP-1571.

EXT-POOL-SERVER.name: Mining Pool Server via Stratum
EXT-POOL-SERVER.rationale: Pool servers distribute work to miners. A malicious pool could send invalid jobs, manipulate difficulty targets, or provide incorrect epoch/extranonce data. No cryptographic authentication of server identity. Maps to EXT-POOL-SERVER from EIP-1571.

EXT-STRATUM-PARTICIPANT.name: Stratum Protocol Participant
EXT-STRATUM-PARTICIPANT.rationale: Either side of the Stratum connection can send malformed JSON, invalid hex formatting, or unauthorized messages. All protocol messages must be validated. Maps to EXT-CLIENT from EIP-1571.

EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER.name: Block Proposer (Miner/Validator)
EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER.entry_point: Block header fields (timestamp, coinbase, difficulty, uncles, PREVRANDAO)
EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER.rationale: Block proposers set block-level context values consumed by EVM opcodes. A malicious proposer can manipulate timestamps (within bounds) to affect difficulty calculations (EIP-100), set PREVRANDAO to influence randomness-dependent contracts, or include uncle references to game issuance. Maps to EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER, EXT-ATTACKER-MINER, EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER from source files.

EXT-ADDRESS-COLLISION-ATTACKER.name: Address Collision Attacker
EXT-ADDRESS-COLLISION-ATTACKER.entry_point: eth_sendRawTransaction with collision address as sender
EXT-ADDRESS-COLLISION-ATTACKER.rationale: Sophisticated attacker with ~2^80 compute resources attempting to find an address collision between an EOA private key and a contract deployment address. EIP-3607 mitigates this by rejecting transactions from addresses with deployed code. Maps to EXT-ATTACKER from EIP-3607.

EXT-DAPP-SIGN-REQUEST.name: DApp via eth_signTypedData RPC
EXT-DAPP-SIGN-REQUEST.rationale: DApps submit structured typed data for signing via EIP-712. Any web application can request signatures. The typed data content could be malicious, misleading, or designed for replay attacks. The wallet must display data accurately and the user must approve.

EXT-PEER-NODE-P2P-HANDSHAKE.name: Peer Node via devp2p eth/64 Handshake
EXT-PEER-NODE-P2P-HANDSHAKE.entry_point: devp2p TCP (eth/64 Status message with forkid)
EXT-PEER-NODE-P2P-HANDSHAKE.rationale: Remote peers in the P2P network are unauthenticated. They provide forkid in Status messages which must be validated against local fork configuration. Malicious peers can lie about fork state to waste connection slots or attempt eclipse attacks.

EXT-PEER-NODE-BLOCK-PROPAGATION.name: Peer Node via P2P Block Propagation
EXT-PEER-NODE-BLOCK-PROPAGATION.rationale: Peers propagate blocks that must be validated against the correct fork rules (Frontier, Homestead, etc.) based on block height. Invalid blocks from wrong fork epoch must be rejected.

EXT-ENR-PEER-SOURCE.name: Peer Node via ENR Exchange
EXT-ENR-PEER-SOURCE.rationale: Peers provide ENR records that must be cryptographically validated: size <= 300 bytes, valid RLP structure, sorted unique keys, valid secp256k1 signature. Even with valid signatures, connectivity information (IP/port) could be stale or intentionally misleading.

EXT-DNS-ENR-SOURCE.name: DNS Discovery Service
EXT-DNS-ENR-SOURCE.rationale: DNS infrastructure providing ENR records for node discovery. Subject to DNS spoofing/hijacking. ENR signatures limit the impact to DoS (directing to wrong IPs) but cannot prevent connectivity disruption.

EXT-ENS-ENR-SOURCE.name: ENS Registry for ENR Resolution
EXT-ENS-ENR-SOURCE.rationale: ENS-based ENR discovery depends on on-chain data integrity. While on-chain data is harder to tamper with, the resolver path may introduce vulnerabilities. ENR signatures provide cryptographic binding regardless.

EXT-ATTACKER-SIG-REPLAY.name: Attacker Replaying EIP-712 Signatures
EXT-ATTACKER-SIG-REPLAY.rationale: Attacker who captures valid EIP-712 signatures can attempt replay attacks. Domain separator provides cross-contract/cross-chain protection, but same-domain replay requires application-level nonce tracking (not part of EIP-712 standard).

EXT-P2P-LC-DATA-SOURCE.name: P2P Peers Serving Light Client Data
EXT-P2P-LC-DATA-SOURCE.entry_point: P2P network (light client update messages in pre-fork format)
EXT-P2P-LC-DATA-SOURCE.rationale: During the Electra fork transition, peers may serve light client data in pre-fork (Deneb) format. This data must be locally upgraded using upgrade functions and validated cryptographically. Merkle branches must be normalized to Electra depth.

EXT-CL-PEER-NODE-P2P.name: CL Peer Node via libp2p Gossip/ReqResp
EXT-CL-PEER-NODE-P2P.entry_point: libp2p gossipsub topics (beacon_block, beacon_attestation, blob_sidecar) and req/resp protocols (BeaconBlocksByRange, BlobSidecarsByRange)
EXT-CL-PEER-NODE-P2P.rationale: CL P2P peers are unauthenticated. They can send invalid beacon blocks, malformed attestations, blob sidecars exceeding limits, or oversized req/resp requests. Covers EXT-PEER-NODE and EXT-REQUESTING-PEER from Electra P2P subgraphs.

EXT-BLOB-NETWORK-P2P.name: P2P Blob Sidecar Network
EXT-BLOB-NETWORK-P2P.entry_point: Blob sidecar retrieval via P2P (blob_sidecar subnets, BlobSidecarsByRange/Root)
EXT-BLOB-NETWORK-P2P.rationale: Blob data is retrieved from unauthenticated P2P peers. Blobs may be withheld, invalid, or have failing KZG proofs. Data availability depends on honest majority of peers.

EXT-EXECUTION-ENGINE-API.name: Execution Engine via Engine API
EXT-EXECUTION-ENGINE-API.rationale: Authenticated via JWT. The EL provides execution payloads and blobs_bundle to proposing validators. Content must be validated (KZG commitments, blob integrity). Covers EXT-EXECUTION-ENGINE from Deneb validator subgraph.

EXT-VALIDATOR-CL.name: Validator via Beacon API / P2P
EXT-VALIDATOR-CL.entry_point: BLSToExecutionChange submission, voluntary exit submission, attestation submission
EXT-VALIDATOR-CL.rationale: Validators submit signed messages but are untrusted. They may submit conflicting withdrawal credential changes, invalid exit signatures, or try to exploit the extended attestation inclusion window.

EXT-MALICIOUS-PEER-COMPRESSION.name: Malicious Peer via Crafted Compressed Payload
EXT-MALICIOUS-PEER-COMPRESSION.rationale: Attacker can send crafted Snappy payloads designed as decompression bombs (small compressed size, huge decompressed size). Size validation against 16MB limit and varint overflow checks are critical defenses.

EXT-PEER-NODE-P2P-DEVP2P.name: Peer Node via devp2p
EXT-PEER-NODE-P2P-DEVP2P.rationale: Peer nodes communicate over unauthenticated P2P network. Any peer can send false transaction announcements with spoofed sender addresses and nonces (EIP-8077), invalid blocks, or malicious data. No authentication required.

EXT-TX-SUBMITTER-RPC.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC
EXT-TX-SUBMITTER-RPC.rationale: Covers all transaction submissions including typed transactions (EIP-2718), blob transactions (EIP-4844/Cancun), and legacy transactions. Unauthenticated public endpoint. Full validation required: type detection, RLP decoding, signature verification, fee validation, blob gas limits, versioned hash validity, init code size limits.

EXT-PEER-NODE-DAS-CUSTODIAN.name: Peer Column Custodian via P2P
EXT-PEER-NODE-DAS-CUSTODIAN.rationale: Peer nodes that custody columns respond to DAS sampling requests over unauthenticated P2P. They may withhold data, provide invalid column proofs, or manipulate node ID assignment to concentrate custody.

EXT-SYNC-COMMITTEE-PEER.name: Sync Committee Subnet Peer via gossip
EXT-SYNC-COMMITTEE-PEER.rationale: Validators on sync committee subnets publish messages over P2P gossip. Peers may submit false sync committee messages, attempt to manipulate aggregation, or delay messages to degrade light client security.

EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER-P2P.name: Block Producer (Validator) via P2P
EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER-P2P.rationale: Validators producing blocks with EIP-1559 base fees, gas limits, and transaction receipts (EIP-658). All block-level fields must be independently validated: base fee calculation, gas limit bounds, gas used, receipt status codes.

EXT-CONTRACT-DEPLOYER-RPC.name: Contract Deployer via JSON-RPC / Transaction
EXT-CONTRACT-DEPLOYER-RPC.entry_point: Contract creation transactions (CREATE, EOFCREATE, initcode transactions)
EXT-CONTRACT-DEPLOYER-RPC.rationale: Deployers submit contract creation transactions. EOF containers (EIP-7692) must be fully validated at deploy time. Malicious deployers may craft bytecode attempting to bypass validation, exploit stack analysis, or trigger edge cases in CALLF/RETF/JUMPF handling.

EXT-EL-ENGINE-API.name: Execution Layer via Engine API
EXT-EL-ENGINE-API.rationale: EL provides execution payload validation results back to CL. JWT-authenticated channel. CL uses EL validation status to make fork choice decisions. Incorrect validation results could compromise consensus.

EXT-NETWORK-PEER-CL-GOSSIP.name: Network Peer via CL Gossip
EXT-NETWORK-PEER-CL-GOSSIP.rationale: CL peers propagate blocks and attestations over unauthenticated P2P gossip. Peers may send invalid blocks, conflicting attestations, or attempt eclipse attacks. All received data must be fully validated.

EXT-RPC-CLIENT-QUERY.name: RPC Client via JSON-RPC (queries)
EXT-RPC-CLIENT-QUERY.rationale: External clients querying receipts (EIP-658 status codes) and logs (bloom filter lookups). Unauthenticated read path. Query parameters could be crafted to cause resource exhaustion.

EXT-DAPP-WALLET-RPC.name: dApp via Wallet JSON-RPC (EIP-2255)
EXT-DAPP-WALLET-RPC.rationale: dApps request wallet permissions via JSON-RPC. Completely untrusted — any website can request permissions. Security relies on user consent prompts, invoker identification, caveat validation, and SSRF protection for URLs in permission requests. Potential for clickjacking, permission over-granting, and SSRF attacks.

EXT-RPC-ENDPOINT-DAPP-PROVIDED.name: DApp-Provided RPC Endpoint
EXT-RPC-ENDPOINT-DAPP-PROVIDED.entry_point: HTTP/HTTPS connection to external RPC server (via EIP-2015 chain switching)
EXT-RPC-ENDPOINT-DAPP-PROVIDED.rationale: RPC endpoints provided by DApps in wallet_updateEthereumChain requests are fully untrusted. The wallet connects to these endpoints to verify chainId. SSRF risk: URL may point to internal services. Response may be spoofed. Must validate URL format, block private IPs, verify net_version and eth_chainId responses match claimed chain.

EXT-BUILDER-GOSSIP.name: Execution Payload Builder via P2P Gossip
EXT-BUILDER-GOSSIP.rationale: Builders submit signed bids via gossipsub. Fully untrusted: bids may reference incorrect parent hashes, claim amounts exceeding builder balance, or carry invalid signatures. After bid acceptance, the builder is delegated responsibility to broadcast DataColumnSidecars but may fail to do so. Validation required: signature verification, builder balance coverage check, parent hash consistency, and bid validity checks.

EXT-GOSSIP-NETWORK-DAS.name: Gossipsub Network (DAS Column Distribution)
EXT-GOSSIP-NETWORK-DAS.rationale: DataColumnSidecars are distributed via gossipsub. Peers on the network are unauthenticated and may send invalid sidecars, withhold data, or flood with garbage. All received columns must be verified against KZG commitments and proofs before acceptance.

EXT-COLUMN-CUSTODY-PEERS.name: Column Custody Peers via Req/Resp
EXT-COLUMN-CUSTODY-PEERS.entry_point: P2P Network (req/resp protocol for column retrieval)
EXT-COLUMN-CUSTODY-PEERS.rationale: When columns are not received via gossip, nodes fall back to direct req/resp queries to peers who custody the needed columns. These peers are untrusted: they may serve invalid data, refuse to respond, or provide columns with invalid KZG proofs. All received data must pass KZG proof verification.

EXT-LIGHT-CLIENT-CONSUMER.name: Light Client via Light Client API
EXT-LIGHT-CLIENT-CONSUMER.rationale: Light clients request headers from full nodes. From the full node's perspective, light client requests are untrusted and may attempt resource exhaustion. From the light client's perspective, the full node serving headers is untrusted and may provide fabricated execution payload headers. Merkle branch proofs must be verified against trusted beacon block body roots.

EXT-UNTRUSTED-KZG-INPUT.name: Untrusted Byte Input for KZG Operations
EXT-UNTRUSTED-KZG-INPUT.entry_point: KZG precompile / verification functions (blob transactions, point evaluation)
EXT-UNTRUSTED-KZG-INPUT.rationale: Raw byte inputs to KZG cryptographic operations (48-byte G1 points, 32-byte field elements, proof verification inputs) originate from transactions and peer-provided data. All inputs are untrusted: G1 points must be validated on the BLS12-381 curve, field elements must be checked against the BLS modulus, and input lengths must be asserted before cryptographic operations.

EXT-USER-JSON-RPC-TX.name: User via JSON-RPC (Transaction Submission)
EXT-USER-JSON-RPC-TX.rationale: Any user or DApp can submit transactions via public JSON-RPC. Transactions may contain crafted precompile inputs (ECRECOVER, ModExp, identity) or malformed access lists. No authentication required.

EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER-PRECOMPILE.name: Contract Caller via CALL to Precompile
EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER-PRECOMPILE.rationale: Any contract can invoke the BLAKE2F precompile with arbitrary input. The precompile must validate exact 213-byte input length and valid final flag (0 or 1). Gas is charged dynamically based on rounds parameter, preventing resource exhaustion.

EXT-DOS-ATTACKER-MODEXP.name: DoS Attacker via ModExp Spam
EXT-DOS-ATTACKER-MODEXP.rationale: Attacker may attempt to submit many cheap ModExp calls to exhaust node resources. EIP-2565 mitigates with minimum gas floor of 200 and repriced gas formula, but the attack vector remains relevant.

EXT-PEER-P2P-BLOCK.name: Network Peer via P2P (Block Propagation)
EXT-PEER-P2P-BLOCK.rationale: Peer nodes propagate blocks over unauthenticated P2P network. Blocks may contain invalid structure, incorrect state transitions, or malformed access lists. Full validation required.

EXT-NODE-OPERATOR-CLI.name: Node Operator via CLI (WS Checkpoint)
EXT-NODE-OPERATOR-CLI.rationale: Node operator provides weak subjectivity checkpoint at startup. Authenticated via local CLI access (physical/SSH), but the checkpoint content itself must be validated against the canonical chain. If the operator provides a checkpoint from an attacker fork, the node will follow the wrong chain.

EXT-LONG-RANGE-ATTACKER.name: Long-Range Attacker via P2P
EXT-LONG-RANGE-ATTACKER.rationale: Adversary presenting a conflicting chain forked from an old finalized checkpoint. Weak subjectivity mechanism defends against this within the WS period. Derived from EXT-ATTACKER in spec_b7dca68c.

EXT-PEER-P2P-DATA-COLUMN.name: Network Peer via P2P (Data Column Sidecars)
EXT-PEER-P2P-DATA-COLUMN.rationale: Peers propagate data column sidecars over unauthenticated gossipsub. Each sidecar requires KZG batch verification and inclusion proof verification before acceptance. Invalid data could cause reconstruction failures or consensus divergence.

EXT-PEER-VIA-P2P.name: Network Peer via P2P (devp2p)
EXT-PEER-VIA-P2P.entry_point: P2P Network (devp2p) - block propagation, eth/68 NewPooledTransactionHashes
EXT-PEER-VIA-P2P.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the network and submit blocks or transaction announcements. Peers may lie about transaction types/sizes in eth/68 announcements. All data must be fully validated.

EXT-DEPOSITOR-VIA-TX.name: Depositor via Deposit Contract
EXT-DEPOSITOR-VIA-TX.entry_point: Deposit Contract deposit() function via EL transaction
EXT-DEPOSITOR-VIA-TX.rationale: Any entity can call the deposit contract with arbitrary pubkey, signature, and withdrawal credentials. The contract performs only minimal validation (data root check, amount check). BLS signature verification is deferred to the beacon chain. Invalid deposits result in burned ETH.

EXT-RPC-PROVIDER.name: Third-Party RPC Provider
EXT-RPC-PROVIDER.rationale: RPC providers are third-party services that may be compromised or malicious. EIP-7919 explicitly addresses this by requiring cryptographic proofs for all responses. Data must be verified against known state roots.

EXT-LIGHT-CLIENT.name: Light Client via RPC
EXT-LIGHT-CLIENT.rationale: Light clients query logs without running a full node. They are untrusted consumers of EL data, but the system must serve them correct and complete data with proofs.

EXT-DAPP-VIA-WALLET-RPC.name: DApp via Wallet JSON-RPC
EXT-DAPP-VIA-WALLET-RPC.rationale: DApps request signatures from wallets. A malicious DApp could request signatures for fraudulent purposes. The wallet must display the validator address and data for user approval. Domain separation via EIP-191 prefix prevents cross-validator signature reuse.

EXT-SIGNATURE-PRESENTER.name: Signature Presenter via Contract Call
EXT-SIGNATURE-PRESENTER.entry_point: Smart contract function call presenting signature for verification (EIP-7749 validator)
EXT-SIGNATURE-PRESENTER.rationale: Any entity can present a signature to a validator contract for verification. The validator must reconstruct the expected message using its own address, hash it, and recover the signer via ecrecover. Untrusted input.

EXT-MINER-VIA-BLOCK.name: Block Producer via P2P
EXT-MINER-VIA-BLOCK.entry_point: P2P Network - block submission with PoW (Homestead) or PoS proposal
EXT-MINER-VIA-BLOCK.rationale: Miners/validators produce blocks that must be fully validated: header, ommers, transactions, state roots, PoW difficulty target. A malicious miner could submit blocks with invalid PoW, incorrect difficulty, or manipulated timestamps.

EXT-P2P-PEER-EL.name: P2P Peer Node via devp2p
EXT-P2P-PEER-EL.rationale: Peer nodes propagate blocks over unauthenticated P2P network. Blocks may contain invalid headers, malformed transactions, or crafted payloads. Covers EXT-P2P-PEER from Prague block header subgraph.

EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER-CL.name: Block Proposer via P2P Network
EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER-CL.entry_point: P2P gossip (BeaconBlock with ExecutionPayload containing Verkle witness)
EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER-CL.rationale: Block proposers submit blocks via the P2P gossip network. A malicious validator could propose blocks with invalid execution payloads or crafted Verkle witnesses. All content must be validated through the full consensus and execution verification pipeline.

EXT-SMART-CONTRACT-EL.name: Smart Contract via EVM CALL
EXT-SMART-CONTRACT-EL.rationale: Smart contracts invoke precompiles with arbitrary calldata. Malicious contracts may supply invalid field elements, points not on curve, points not in subgroup, or attempt gas exhaustion via large MSM/pairing inputs.

EXT-DISCOVERY-PEER.name: Peer Node via Discovery Protocol
EXT-DISCOVERY-PEER.rationale: Discovery protocol peers are unauthenticated. They may attempt amplification attacks via ENRRequest without prior ping exchange, send forged ENR records, or manipulate sequence numbers.

EXT-NODE-OPERATOR-CL.name: Node Operator via Local Configuration
EXT-NODE-OPERATOR-CL.entry_point: Local broadcast file loading (BLSToExecutionChange broadcast file)
EXT-NODE-OPERATOR-CL.rationale: Node operators load broadcast files locally. While they have local system access (semi-trusted channel), the file content originates from a community repository and must be validated. Malicious or corrupt broadcast files could cause rejection of legitimate messages.

EXT-CALLER-PRECOMPILE.name: Contract/EOA via EVM CALL to Precompile
EXT-CALLER-PRECOMPILE.rationale: Any contract or EOA can invoke precompiles via EVM call opcodes. Input data is arbitrary and untrusted. Gas metering is the primary protection against abuse.

EXT-PROOF-PROVIDER-P2P.name: Merkle Proof Provider via P2P / Light Client Protocol
EXT-PROOF-PROVIDER-P2P.entry_point: P2P light client protocol (single and multi-item Merkle proofs)
EXT-PROOF-PROVIDER-P2P.rationale: External peers providing Merkle proofs are unauthenticated. Proofs must be cryptographically verified against a trusted root. Malicious peers can provide forged proofs.

EXT-L2-ROLLUP-SYSTEM.name: L2 Rollup via RIP Transaction Types
EXT-L2-ROLLUP-SYSTEM.entry_point: Transaction type namespace 0x40-0x7f (EIP-7808 RIP reserved range)
EXT-L2-ROLLUP-SYSTEM.rationale: L2 rollups define their own transaction types in the reserved range. L1 nodes must not process these as EIP types. No authentication of RIP governance decisions at the protocol level.

EXT-VALIDATOR-ATTESTATION.name: Validator via Attestation Gossip
EXT-VALIDATOR-ATTESTATION.rationale: Validators submit attestations via P2P gossip. Committee membership must be verified to prevent gossip mutation attacks (EIP-7549). Aggregated signatures require pairing-based verification.

EXT-GOSSIP-PEER-P2P.name: Gossip Network Peer via P2P
EXT-GOSSIP-PEER-P2P.entry_point: P2P gossip protocol (attestation propagation, EIP-7045 extended gossip conditions)
EXT-GOSSIP-PEER-P2P.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. They may propagate stale or malicious attestations. Extended gossip window increases exposure to attestation flooding.

EXT-P2P-PEERS-OPTSYNC.name: P2P Peers via Beacon Block Gossip (Optimistic Sync)
EXT-P2P-PEERS-OPTSYNC.entry_point: P2P beacon block gossip (blocks imported optimistically before EL validation)
EXT-P2P-PEERS-OPTSYNC.rationale: Peers providing beacon blocks are unauthenticated. Optimistic sync imports blocks before execution validation, creating a window where fork choice may include invalid blocks.

EXT-ATTACKER-OPTSYNC.name: Malicious Block Producer via P2P
EXT-ATTACKER-OPTSYNC.entry_point: P2P beacon block gossip (crafted blocks with invalid execution payloads)
EXT-ATTACKER-OPTSYNC.rationale: Attacker crafts blocks with unreferenceable parent hashes to trigger false justification and poison fork choice. SAFE_SLOTS_TO_IMPORT_OPTIMISTICALLY (128) provides mitigation window.

EXT-GENESIS-CONFIG-FILE.name: Genesis Configuration File via Filesystem
EXT-GENESIS-CONFIG-FILE.entry_point: Filesystem read of assets/ directory JSON configuration
EXT-GENESIS-CONFIG-FILE.rationale: Genesis file is loaded from local filesystem, implying some trust in the deployment environment. However, content must be validated (hex parsing, address format) as it could be corrupted or tampered.

EXT-VALIDATOR-CLIENT-HTTP.name: Validator Client via HTTP API
EXT-VALIDATOR-CLIENT-HTTP.entry_point: HTTP POST /sign/:identifier (EIP-3030 BLS Remote Signer API)
EXT-VALIDATOR-CLIENT-HTTP.rationale: HTTP requests arrive over the network. Even with TLS, the signer must authenticate requests, validate BLS domain, check rate limits. Unauthorized signing could cause slashing.

EXT-HSM-SECRETS.name: HSM or Secrets Manager
EXT-HSM-SECRETS.entry_point: Key retrieval API (EIP-3030 BLS key storage backend)
EXT-HSM-SECRETS.rationale: HSM/secrets manager is a controlled dependency with authenticated access, but key integrity depends on correct HSM configuration. A misconfigured HSM could expose keys.

EXT-UNTRUSTED-NETWORK-HTTP.name: Untrusted Network for BLS Signer
EXT-UNTRUSTED-NETWORK-HTTP.entry_point: Network layer carrying HTTP requests to BLS remote signer (EIP-3030)
EXT-UNTRUSTED-NETWORK-HTTP.rationale: Without TLS, the network exposes signing requests and responses to eavesdropping and MITM attacks. Even with TLS, network-level DoS is possible.

EXT-ATTACKER-RPC.name: Malicious Actor via JSON-RPC
EXT-ATTACKER-RPC.rationale: Attacker exploiting exposed RPC for reconnaissance (EIP-7910 config leak), DDoS via repeated requests, or replaying EIP-7702 authorization tuples. No authentication required.

EXT-NETWORK-PEER-P2P.name: Network Peer via P2P (devp2p / libp2p)
EXT-NETWORK-PEER-P2P.rationale: Peer nodes on the P2P network are unauthenticated and may be malicious. They can send invalid blocks, malformed transactions, or attempt eclipse attacks. All received data must be independently validated. Applies to both EL devp2p peers and CL libp2p peers.

EXT-REQUESTING-PEER-P2P.name: Requesting Peer via P2P Request/Response
EXT-REQUESTING-PEER-P2P.rationale: Unauthenticated peers requesting blob data. Must enforce rate limits and retention window checks (MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS). Potential for resource exhaustion.

EXT-FULL-NODE-BEACON-API.name: Full Node via Beacon API
EXT-FULL-NODE-BEACON-API.rationale: Full nodes serving light client data are untrusted. Bootstrap data, updates, and finality updates must be verified against trusted block roots and sync committee signatures. A compromised node could serve stale or false data.

EXT-MALICIOUS-NODE-RPC.name: Compromised Node via eth_config RPC
EXT-MALICIOUS-NODE-RPC.rationale: A malicious or compromised node queried for configuration comparison (EIP-7910) can return false configuration data, misleading validators about fork readiness.

EXT-UNTRUSTED-CONTRACT-EVM.name: Untrusted External Contract via EVM CALL
EXT-UNTRUSTED-CONTRACT-EVM.rationale: External contracts invoked via CALL may contain malicious code attempting re-entrancy, state modification in static context, or adversarial precompile inputs. STATICCALL (EIP-214) provides sandboxing. EIP-7702 delegation introduces new attack surface where delegated code executes in EOA context.

EXT-TX-SUBMITTER-TYPE4.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC (Type-4)
EXT-TX-SUBMITTER-TYPE4.rationale: Submitter of EIP-7702 type-4 transactions. Authorization tuples must be validated: chain ID, nonce bounds, signature recovery, s-value malleability, authority code state. Invalid authorizations are skipped (not reverted), but format validation is strict.

EXT-ATTACKER-AUTH-REPLAY.name: Attacker Replaying EIP-7702 Authorizations
EXT-ATTACKER-AUTH-REPLAY.entry_point: JSON-RPC API (replayed authorization tuples in type-4 transactions)
EXT-ATTACKER-AUTH-REPLAY.rationale: Attacker attempting to replay previously signed authorization tuples. Nonce-based replay protection ensures nonce mismatch causes skip. Cross-chain replay possible if chain_id=0 was used.

EXT-EXTERNAL-DATA-SOURCE.name: External Historical Data Source
EXT-EXTERNAL-DATA-SOURCE.entry_point: e2store archive / Portal Network / EIP-7801 DevP2P protocol
EXT-EXTERNAL-DATA-SOURCE.rationale: After EIP-7927 history expiry, pre-merge data is retrieved from external sources. Data must be validated against known block hashes. Untrusted sources could serve manipulated historical data.

EXT-PEER-P2P-DEVP2P.name: Peer Node via devp2p
EXT-PEER-P2P-DEVP2P.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the network and send arbitrary messages including malformed transactions, invalid blobs, or fabricated blob data. Covers EIP-8094 blob separation and general tx propagation.

EXT-PEER-P2P-CL-GOSSIP.name: Peer Node via CL Gossip
EXT-PEER-P2P-CL-GOSSIP.entry_point: libp2p gossipsub (beacon blocks, attestations, P2P fork-versioned messages)
EXT-PEER-P2P-CL-GOSSIP.rationale: CL peers are unauthenticated at the network level. Covers EIP-7928 fork version selection and general CL P2P messaging. Malicious peers can send messages with wrong fork versions.

EXT-MEV-RELAY.name: External MEV-Boost Relay (Archetypal)
EXT-MEV-RELAY.entry_point: MEV-Boost relay API / External builder API
EXT-MEV-RELAY.rationale: Archetypal attack vector: MEV-Boost relays and external block builders are untrusted third-party services that could provide incorrect execution payloads, censor transactions, or perform denial of service. Data from relays must be independently verified.

EXT-BLOCK-BUILDER.name: Block Builder via MEV Relay
EXT-BLOCK-BUILDER.rationale: Builders submit execution payload bids competing in block auctions. Builders are untrusted — they may submit invalid payloads, undervalued bids, or attempt censorship. The relay is expected to validate builder submissions.

EXT-MEV-SEARCHER.name: MEV Searcher via Builder
EXT-MEV-SEARCHER.rationale: Searchers identify MEV opportunities and submit bundles. They are untrusted external actors who may attempt sandwich attacks, front-running, or other extractive strategies.

EXT-SLASHING-REPORTER.name: Slashing Evidence Reporter via Beacon Block
EXT-SLASHING-REPORTER.entry_point: ProposerSlashing / AttesterSlashing operations in beacon blocks
EXT-SLASHING-REPORTER.rationale: Any validator can include slashing evidence in blocks. The evidence itself must be cryptographically verified — the reporter is untrusted but evidence validity is independently checkable.

EXT-WEBAUTHN-DEVICE.name: WebAuthn/FIDO2 Device via Smart Contract
EXT-WEBAUTHN-DEVICE.rationale: External hardware devices generate secp256r1 signatures that are passed through smart contracts to the precompile. The signature data is untrusted — all cryptographic validation (input length, curve membership, bounds checks) must be performed. Covers EIP-7951.

EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER-POW.name: Block Producer/Miner via P2P (PoW context)
EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER-POW.entry_point: P2P network (block headers with difficulty claims)
EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER-POW.rationale: In PoW context (EIP-2384 Muir Glacier), miners produce blocks with stated difficulty. Block difficulty must be independently recalculated and verified against the difficulty formula. A miner could attempt to submit blocks with incorrect difficulty.

EXT-ATTESTING-VALIDATOR.name: Attesting Validator via P2P Gossip
EXT-ATTESTING-VALIDATOR.entry_point: Indexed attestations via P2P gossip (fork choice on_attestation handler)
EXT-ATTESTING-VALIDATOR.rationale: Validators submit attestations that influence fork choice head selection via LMD GHOST weight calculation. Malicious validators can submit conflicting attestations (equivocation), target incorrect checkpoints, or attempt balancing attacks. Attestation target, source, consistency, and equivocation status must be verified.

EXT-LIGHT-CLIENT-PEER.name: Light Client Peer via P2P
EXT-LIGHT-CLIENT-PEER.rationale: Light clients requesting Deneb-format headers with blob gas fields from full nodes. From the full node perspective, light client requests are untrusted and could be used for resource exhaustion.

EXT-ETH1-DEPOSIT-CONTRACT.name: ETH1 Deposit Contract via Merkle Proof
EXT-ETH1-DEPOSIT-CONTRACT.entry_point: Deposit operations in beacon blocks (Merkle proof against eth1_data.deposit_root)
EXT-ETH1-DEPOSIT-CONTRACT.rationale: The deposit contract is a deployed smart contract whose state is cryptographically verified via Merkle proofs. The contract itself is trusted (immutable code), but deposit data must be validated: Merkle proof verification, BLS signature check over DepositMessage. Invalid BLS signatures result in unusable validator records.

EXT-PEER-P2P-EL.name: Network Peer via devp2p
EXT-PEER-P2P-EL.rationale: P2P peers propagate blocks to the EL for state transition processing (Cancun fork). Blocks from peers must pass full validation: header consensus rules, body execution, Merkle root verification. Any peer can send invalid blocks.

EXT-BEACON-CHAIN-VIA-ENGINE-API.name: Beacon Chain via Engine API (Withdrawals)
EXT-BEACON-CHAIN-VIA-ENGINE-API.entry_point: Engine API (withdrawal processing in block body)
EXT-BEACON-CHAIN-VIA-ENGINE-API.rationale: The CL provides withdrawal data to the EL for balance crediting. Authenticated via JWT. Withdrawal amounts are converted to Wei and credited to recipients. The EL trusts the CL for withdrawal validity but must correctly apply state changes (balance increases, trie updates).

EXT-CALLER-CONTRACT-KZG.name: Calling Contract via EVM CALL to Point Evaluation Precompile
EXT-CALLER-CONTRACT-KZG.rationale: Any contract can invoke the KZG point evaluation precompile with arbitrary input. Input must be exactly 192 bytes. Versioned hash, field elements (z, y < BLS_MODULUS), commitment, and proof must all be validated. The precompile must reject malformed inputs and invalid proofs. Fixed gas cost of 50000.

EXT-BLOB-DATA-SOURCE.name: Blob Data Source via P2P Network
EXT-BLOB-DATA-SOURCE.entry_point: Blob data delivery via P2P (for KZG commitment verification)
EXT-BLOB-DATA-SOURCE.rationale: Network peers or local storage provide blob data alongside commitments and proofs for verification. Blob-specific verification derives evaluation challenges deterministically via Fiat-Shamir. Blob field elements must be < BLS_MODULUS. Invalid blobs must be rejected.

EXT-TX-SUBMITTER-CALLDATA.name: Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC
EXT-TX-SUBMITTER-CALLDATA.rationale: Users submit transactions with arbitrary calldata amounts. EIP-7623 introduces a gas floor for data-heavy transactions (10 gas per token vs standard 4). All transactions must have gas limit >= max(standard_gas, floor_gas). Transaction submitters are untrusted and may attempt to exploit calldata pricing.

EXT-BLOB-SUBMITTER.name: Blob Data Submitter
EXT-BLOB-SUBMITTER.entry_point: Blob submission for KZG commitment generation
EXT-BLOB-SUBMITTER.rationale: External entities provide raw blob data (131,072 bytes = 4096 field elements) for commitment. Each field element must be < BLS_MODULUS. The commitment is a G1 point computed via linear combination of Lagrange basis points. Blob submitters are untrusted; all field element validation is required.

EXT-PROOF-PROVIDER.name: KZG Proof Provider via P2P or Block
EXT-PROOF-PROVIDER.rationale: Block proposers or peers provide KZG proofs for verification. Proofs consist of G1 curve points that must pass KeyValidate checks (identity point 0xc0... is permitted). Verification uses bilinear pairing on BLS12-381. Batch verification uses Fiat-Shamir random challenges with RCKZGBATCH___V1_ domain separation.

EXT-BLOB-DATA-SOURCE-DENEB.name: Blob Data Source for Verification
EXT-BLOB-DATA-SOURCE-DENEB.entry_point: Blob-specific KZG verification (verify_blob_kzg_proof with Fiat-Shamir challenge)
EXT-BLOB-DATA-SOURCE-DENEB.rationale: Network peers or local storage provide blob data alongside commitments and proofs. Blob verification derives evaluation challenges deterministically via Fiat-Shamir (FSBLOBVERIFY_V1_ domain). Polynomial evaluated at challenge using barycentric interpolation over roots of unity. Data source is untrusted.

EXT-RPC-CLIENT.name: User/DApp via JSON-RPC
EXT-RPC-CLIENT.entry_point: JSON-RPC API (eth_getBalance, eth_getStorageAt, eth_call, eth_getCode with EIP-1898 block parameters)
EXT-RPC-CLIENT.rationale: JSON-RPC is a public, unauthenticated interface. Clients can submit arbitrary block parameters including malformed objects (both blockNumber and blockHash present), non-existent block hashes, or references to non-canonical blocks. All parameter formats must be validated.

EXT-PEER-NODE-ETH69.name: Remote Peer via eth/69 Protocol
EXT-PEER-NODE-ETH69.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. Peers may advertise false history ranges (earliestBlock/latestBlock), send malformed status messages, or provide corrupted receipts without bloom filters. Range claims are unverified until blocks are actually requested.

EXT-PEER-NODE-ETH70.name: Remote Peer via eth/70 P2P
EXT-PEER-NODE-ETH70.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. Can send malformed, incomplete, or malicious receipt data. Covers EXT-PEER-NODE, EXT-REQUESTING-PEER from source subgraphs.

EXT-PEER-NODE-FULU-DAS.name: P2P Network Peers (Column Sidecar Sources)
EXT-PEER-NODE-FULU-DAS.entry_point: P2P column sidecar gossip and req-resp (Fulu DAS)
EXT-PEER-NODE-FULU-DAS.rationale: Column sidecar providers are unauthenticated P2P peers. They may withhold specific columns to prevent data availability verification, provide sidecars with invalid KZG proofs, or delay responses beyond MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS. All sidecars must be structurally verified and KZG-proof-checked.

EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER-FULU.name: Block Proposer via P2P Network (Fulu)
EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER-FULU.entry_point: Signed beacon block via P2P gossip for fork choice processing
EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER-FULU.rationale: Block proposers submit signed beacon blocks for fork choice processing. A malicious proposer may submit blocks with unavailable data (columns not published), triggering the queuing mechanism. Blocks must pass parent validation, slot validation, finality checks, and DAS-based data availability before acceptance.

EXT-PEER-P2P-NETWORK.name: Peer Node via P2P Network
EXT-PEER-P2P-NETWORK.entry_point: P2P devp2p protocol (NewBlock, NewBlockHashes, block/tx gossip)
EXT-PEER-P2P-NETWORK.rationale: Network peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the P2P network and send arbitrary blocks, transactions, or messages. Covers EXT-NETWORK-PEER, EXT-PEER-NODE from Frontier, EIP-3675, EIP-4345, EIP-225.

EXT-USER-GRAPHQL.name: User/DApp via GraphQL API
EXT-USER-GRAPHQL.entry_point: GraphQL API on port 8547 (/graphql endpoint, sendRawTransaction mutation)
EXT-USER-GRAPHQL.rationale: GraphQL API is unauthenticated by default per EIP-1767. No built-in rate limiting or access control. Covers EXT-CLIENT, EXT-TRANSACTION-SUBMITTER, EXT-API-CLIENT from EIP-1767.

EXT-DNS-RESOLVER.name: DNS Resolver via DNS Protocol
EXT-DNS-RESOLVER.entry_point: DNS TXT record resolution (EIP-1459 enrtree protocol)
EXT-DNS-RESOLVER.rationale: DNS infrastructure is untrusted. Responses may be spoofed, corrupted, or served by compromised resolvers. Signature verification provides integrity but DNS itself is untrusted.

EXT-POW-MINER.name: PoW Miner via P2P Network
EXT-POW-MINER.rationale: Miners are untrusted network participants. Blocks may have manipulated difficulty, invalid headers, or attempt to trigger premature TTD. Covers EXT-MINER from EIP-3675, EIP-4345.

EXT-CLIQUE-SIGNER.name: Authorized Clique Signer via P2P
EXT-CLIQUE-SIGNER.entry_point: P2P block propagation with ECDSA-signed headers (EIP-225 Clique)
EXT-CLIQUE-SIGNER.rationale: Even authorized Clique signers are untrusted for block content. Signing authorization is verified but block content, votes, and timestamps require full validation. Covers EXT-AUTHORIZED-SIGNER from EIP-225.

EXT-MESSAGE-SIGNER.name: Message Signer via Transaction/Contract Call
EXT-MESSAGE-SIGNER.entry_point: Contract function calls with signed messages (CHAINID-based replay protection)
EXT-MESSAGE-SIGNER.rationale: External users submitting signed messages for contract verification are untrusted. Signatures may originate from different chains (replay attempt). Covers EXT-USER from EIP-1344.

EXT-BUILDER-BID-GOSSIP.name: Builder via Gossip Network
EXT-BUILDER-BID-GOSSIP.entry_point: execution_payload_bid gossip topic, execution_payload gossip topic
EXT-BUILDER-BID-GOSSIP.rationale: Builders submit bids and envelopes via P2P gossip. BLS signatures authenticate builder identity but bid content (value, payload, state_root) requires full validation. Covers EXT-PROPOSER interaction and EXT-BUILDER-DEPOSIT from Gloas.

EXT-BUILDER-DEPOSIT-TX.name: Builder Deposit via EL Transaction
EXT-BUILDER-DEPOSIT-TX.rationale: Builder registration occurs via untrusted EL transactions. Withdrawal credentials format and deposit amounts must be validated. Covers EXT-BUILDER-DEPOSIT from Gloas.

EXT-PEER-P2P-ETH.name: Peer Node via devp2p (eth/65+)
EXT-PEER-P2P-ETH.entry_point: devp2p eth protocol (NewPooledTransactionHashes, GetPooledTransactions, PooledTransactions, blob sidecar gossip, fork ID in ENR/handshake)
EXT-PEER-P2P-ETH.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P network. Peers can send fake transaction hash announcements, return wrong transactions for requested hashes, gossip invalid blob sidecars, or lie about their fork ID. All data requires full validation.

EXT-PEER-DISCOVERY.name: Discovery Network Peer
EXT-PEER-DISCOVERY.rationale: Unauthenticated discovery protocol. Peers advertise fork IDs in ENRs without cryptographic proof of correctness. Fork ID can be spoofed to bypass pre-filtering.

EXT-SYNC-PEER-LC.name: Light Client Sync Source via P2P/Beacon API
EXT-SYNC-PEER-LC.entry_point: Light Client Sync Protocol (LightClientUpdate, LightClientBootstrap messages)
EXT-SYNC-PEER-LC.rationale: Light client servers provide updates containing Merkle proofs and sync committee signatures. Data is unauthenticated and must be verified via fork-aware generalized indices, Merkle branch validation, and sync committee signature verification.

EXT-DATA-COLUMN-PROVIDER.name: Data Column Provider via P2P
EXT-DATA-COLUMN-PROVIDER.entry_point: P2P gossip (DataColumnSidecar containing cells and KZG proofs)
EXT-DATA-COLUMN-PROVIDER.rationale: Nodes providing data column sidecars for data availability sampling. Cells and proofs must be batch-verified via Fiat-Shamir challenge aggregation and BLS12-381 pairing checks. Invalid proofs must be detected and rejected.

EXT-CALLING-CONTRACT.name: Smart Contract via EVM CALL
EXT-CALLING-CONTRACT.entry_point: Precompile call to address 0x0A (point evaluation precompile)
EXT-CALLING-CONTRACT.rationale: Any smart contract can call the point evaluation precompile with arbitrary 192-byte input. The precompile must validate input length, versioned hash format, KZG commitment and proof validity, and field element ranges.

EXT-BLOB-DATA-SUBMITTER.name: Blob Data Submitter via JSON-RPC
EXT-BLOB-DATA-SUBMITTER.entry_point: JSON-RPC API (eth_sendRawTransaction with Type 3 blob tx)
EXT-BLOB-DATA-SUBMITTER.rationale: Submits EIP-4844 blob transactions containing VersionedHash commitments. Unauthenticated, all blob data and KZG commitments must be fully validated.

EXT-CL-VALIDATOR.name: Beacon Chain Validator via P2P Gossip
EXT-CL-VALIDATOR.entry_point: P2P Gossip Network (beacon block proposals, attestations)
EXT-CL-VALIDATOR.rationale: Validators propose blocks and submit attestations over unauthenticated P2P gossip. Any validator may be malicious — proposing invalid blocks, conflicting attestations, or attempting censorship. Covers 'Beacon Chain Validator' entity.

EXT-P2P-GOSSIP-SSZ.name: P2P Peer via Gossip (SSZ Containers)
EXT-P2P-GOSSIP-SSZ.rationale: Peers send SSZ-encoded containers (using EIP-7688 ProgressiveContainer format) over gossip. Containers must be validated for correct field structure, stable merkle roots, and proof integrity. Unauthenticated channel.

EXT-OFFCHAIN-VERIFIER.name: Off-Chain Verifier (Merkle Proof Consumer)
EXT-OFFCHAIN-VERIFIER.rationale: External systems verifying merkle proofs against beacon state. They consume proofs but do not send data into the system. However, proof requests could be crafted to target edge cases in the ProgressiveContainer merkleization.

EXT-SMART-CONTRACT-VERIFIER.name: Smart Contract Verifier (On-Chain Proof Consumer)
EXT-SMART-CONTRACT-VERIFIER.rationale: Smart contracts that verify SSZ merkle proofs on-chain. They rely on stable generalized indices from EIP-7688. Untrusted — contracts may supply malformed proof data.

EXT-DAPP-USER.name: DApp User via Browser
EXT-DAPP-USER.rationale: DApp users interact with wallet providers through browser APIs. User actions trigger wallet selection and provider interaction. Untrusted browser environment.

EXT-HARDWARE-WALLET.name: Hardware Wallet Implementation
EXT-HARDWARE-WALLET.rationale: Hardware wallets sign SSZ containers. EIP-7688 migration affects container structure which hardware wallets must handle correctly. External device with its own firmware — data sent to/from it crosses a trust boundary.

EXT-IL-SUBMITTER-P2P.name: Inclusion List Submitter via P2P Gossip
EXT-IL-SUBMITTER-P2P.rationale: SignedInclusionList messages arrive via unauthenticated P2P gossip. Any peer can submit them. Committee membership, committee root, and BLS signature must all be validated before acceptance.

EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER-PROPOSER.name: Block Producer / Proposer via P2P
EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER-PROPOSER.rationale: Block proposers submit blocks that must satisfy inclusion list compliance. Proposers are validators but their blocks are received via unauthenticated P2P and must be fully validated including IL compliance checks.

EXT-CONTRACT-DEPLOYER-TX.name: Contract Deployer via Transaction
EXT-CONTRACT-DEPLOYER-TX.rationale: Any user can submit contract creation transactions. The init code and resulting bytecode are fully attacker-controlled. EIP-170 size limits prevent DoS via oversized contracts. Covers EXT-DEPLOYER.

EXT-MESSAGE-CALLER.name: Message Caller via Transaction/Internal Call
EXT-MESSAGE-CALLER.rationale: Any external account or contract can initiate message calls. Call data, target address, and value are all untrusted inputs. Jump destination validation and opcode restrictions provide runtime safety.

EXT-P2P-PEER-CL-GOSSIP.name: Peer Node via CL Gossipsub
EXT-P2P-PEER-CL-GOSSIP.rationale: Peer nodes on the P2P gossip network are unauthenticated. All messages (sync committee messages, attestations, contributions) require full validation: slot checks, subnet membership, duplicate detection, BLS signature verification.

EXT-REMOTE-DISCOVERY-NODE.name: Remote Node via Discovery v5 UDP
EXT-REMOTE-DISCOVERY-NODE.rationale: Discovery nodes respond to FINDNODE queries with ENR records. UDP is unauthenticated and unreliable. ENR records must be verified via their embedded signatures. Routing table poisoning and eclipse attacks are possible threat vectors.

EXT-UDP-NETWORK-TRANSPORT.name: UDP Network Transport
EXT-UDP-NETWORK-TRANSPORT.rationale: The underlying UDP transport is unauthenticated, unreliable, and potentially adversarial. Packets require header unmasking, protocol ID verification, and AES-GCM decryption/authentication before processing.

EXT-CL-GOSSIP-PEER.name: Network Peer via CL Gossip (GossipSub)
EXT-CL-GOSSIP-PEER.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P gossip network. Any peer can send messages on subscribed topics. Messages may be malformed, oversized, or maliciously crafted. Peer identity provides no trust guarantee.

EXT-CL-REQRESP-PEER.name: Remote Beacon Node via Req/Resp Protocol
EXT-CL-REQRESP-PEER.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P connection. Peers are discovered via discv5 and connected via libp2p. Fork digest check provides compatibility verification but not trust. Peer may send invalid responses, incorrect status, or attempt resource exhaustion.

EXT-EL-NETWORK-PEER.name: Network Peer via EL P2P (devp2p)
EXT-EL-NETWORK-PEER.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peer sending block headers and bodies. Blocks may have invalid difficulty, incorrect fork rules, or malformed transactions. No authentication mechanism.

EXT-EL-BLOCK-PRODUCER.name: Block Producer (Miner) via P2P
EXT-EL-BLOCK-PRODUCER.rationale: Miners produce blocks with difficulty calculations. A malicious miner could attempt to submit blocks with incorrect difficulty values. Block difficulty must be fully validated against the expected computation.

EXT-CL-VALIDATOR-IL.name: Validator via P2P (Inclusion List Submission)
EXT-CL-VALIDATOR-IL.rationale: Validators submit inclusion lists via P2P. A validator may equivocate by sending conflicting inclusion lists for the same slot. Equivocation detection is required. Lists must arrive before view freeze deadline.

EXT-CL-BLOCK-BUILDER.name: Block Builder (EIP-7805 context)
EXT-CL-BLOCK-BUILDER.entry_point: Block building interface consuming inclusion list transactions
EXT-CL-BLOCK-BUILDER.rationale: Block builders consume inclusion list transactions but may attempt to censor or reorder them. Enforcement mechanism for inclusion is separate from the list submission protocol.

EXT-CL-SSZ-DATA-SOURCE.name: Untrusted SSZ Data Source via P2P/RPC
EXT-CL-SSZ-DATA-SOURCE.entry_point: SSZ deserialization pipeline (P2P messages, RPC responses, stored snapshots)
EXT-CL-SSZ-DATA-SOURCE.rationale: Raw SSZ bytes from any external source are untrusted. Malformed payloads may exploit deserialization: invalid offsets, excess trailing bytes, list capacity violations, invalid union selectors, missing bitlist sentinels, or decompression bombs.

EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER-EVM.name: Smart Contract via EVM CALL
EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER-EVM.entry_point: EVM CALL opcode to precompile addresses (0x05 MODEXP)
EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER-EVM.rationale: Any contract can invoke precompiles with arbitrary input data. Input parsing and gas metering must handle all edge cases. Covers EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER from MODEXP.

EXT-BUILDER-PBS.name: Block Builder via PBS Bid Channel
EXT-BUILDER-PBS.rationale: Builders submit execution payload bids that must be fully validated: BLS signature, builder active status, sufficient balance, matching slot/parent/randao, blob commitment limits. Covers EXT-BUILDER and EXT-BUILDER-OPERATOR from Gloas subgraphs.

EXT-WALLET-EXTENSION-BROWSER.name: Wallet Browser Extension via DOM Events
EXT-WALLET-EXTENSION-BROWSER.rationale: Browser extensions inject code into page context and announce wallet providers via DOM events. Any extension can impersonate legitimate wallets. Provider info (rdns, uuid, icon) cannot be trusted. Covers EXT-WALLET-EXTENSION, EXT-MALICIOUS-EXTENSION, and EXT-WALLET-APP from EIP-6963.

EXT-USER-JSON-RPC-B9.name: User via JSON-RPC (EIP-1474)
EXT-USER-JSON-RPC-B9.entry_point: JSON-RPC API (eth_sendRawTransaction, eth_call, eth_estimateGas, all EIP-1474 methods)
EXT-USER-JSON-RPC-B9.rationale: Users submit transactions and queries via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. All input requires full validation: JSON parsing, RPC structure, method lookup, parameter format (Quantity/Data hex encoding), transaction signature verification. Covers EXT-USER from Shanghai, EXT-TX-SUBMITTER from Prague exceptions, EXT-TX-SUBMITTER and EXT-RPC-CLIENT from EIP-1474, and EXT-TX-SENDER from EIP-6780.

EXT-P2P-PEER-EL-B9.name: P2P Peer Node via devp2p/eth/67
EXT-P2P-PEER-EL-B9.entry_point: P2P Wire Protocol (eth/67 message types, snap protocol)
EXT-P2P-PEER-EL-B9.rationale: Peer nodes send wire protocol messages including blocks, transactions, and state sync data. eth/67 removes GetNodeData/NodeData (0x0d/0x0e); deprecated messages must be rejected. All block data requires full header validation. Covers EXT-PEER from Shanghai and EIP-7918, EXT-PEER-NODE from EIP-4938, and EXT-SNAP-PEER for snap protocol.

EXT-BEACON-API-CLIENT.name: API Client via Beacon REST API
EXT-BEACON-API-CLIENT.entry_point: Beacon Node REST API (HTTP endpoints per OpenAPI 3 spec)
EXT-BEACON-API-CLIENT.rationale: The Beacon API is explicitly warned against public internet exposure. No built-in authentication; security layers (reverse proxy, firewall) are expected at the infrastructure level. Endpoints that trigger heavy computation or return large responses are DoS vectors. Covers EXT-API-CLIENT from Beacon APIs.

EXT-PROOF-ENGINE.name: Proof Generation Engine via Prover API
EXT-PROOF-ENGINE.rationale: The proof engine generates zkEVM execution proofs delivered to the prover endpoint. While typically co-located with the prover, it crosses a trust boundary. Provers MUST validate engine output before signing with BLS. A compromised engine could produce invalid proofs. Covers EXT-PROOF-ENGINE and EXT-PROOF-ENGINE-UNTRUSTED from EIP-8025.

EXT-P2P-GOSSIP-CL-B9.name: P2P Peer via CL Gossip (Execution Proofs)
EXT-P2P-GOSSIP-CL-B9.rationale: SignedExecutionProofs are received from the gossip network. Full validation required: non-empty proof data, proof engine verification, duplicate detection, BLS signature verification against whitelisted prover keys, domain separation check. Covers EXT-GOSSIP-NETWORK from EIP-8025.

EXT-EXECUTION-ENGINE-B9.name: Execution Engine via Engine API (Bellatrix)
EXT-EXECUTION-ENGINE-B9.rationale: Authenticated via JWT. The EL processes fork choice updates and builds payloads. Content must be validated. During merge transition, the CL fetches PoW block data via eth_getBlockByHash. Covers EXT-EXECUTION-ENGINE and EXT-EXECUTION-CLIENT-RPC from Bellatrix fork choice.

EXT-POW-CHAIN.name: PoW Execution Chain via JSON-RPC
EXT-POW-CHAIN.rationale: During the merge transition, the CL fetches terminal PoW block data to validate TERMINAL_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY conditions. The PoW chain data is accessed via the local execution client's JSON-RPC, which is JWT-authenticated. However, the PoW data content (total difficulty, parent total difficulty) must be independently validated against consensus rules. Covers EXT-POW-CHAIN from Bellatrix.

EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER-B9.name: Block Producer (Blob Fee Calculation)
EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER-B9.entry_point: Block header (excess_blob_gas field with EIP-7918 reserve price logic)
EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER-B9.rationale: Block producers compute excess_blob_gas using the modified reserve price formula. Validators must independently recalculate and verify the header value matches. Incorrect reserve price calculations or manipulated base_fee could distort blob pricing. Covers EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER from EIP-7918.

EXT-CALLER-CONTRACT-EVM.name: Calling Contract via EVM CALL
EXT-CALLER-CONTRACT-EVM.rationale: Any contract can invoke precompiles with arbitrary input data. Gas metering is the primary defense. Consolidates EXT-CALLER-CONTRACT and EXT-CALLER.

EXT-END-USER.name: End User via Wallet UI
EXT-END-USER.entry_point: Wallet approval/rejection prompts (transaction signing, DID auth consent)
EXT-END-USER.rationale: Users may be social-engineered into approving malicious transactions. User consent is a trust boundary but not a guarantee of correctness.

EXT-ETHEREUM-NODE-BACKEND.name: Ethereum Node via JSON-RPC Backend
EXT-ETHEREUM-NODE-BACKEND.entry_point: JSON-RPC responses from remote node to provider
EXT-ETHEREUM-NODE-BACKEND.rationale: DApp-connected nodes may be untrusted third-party services. Response data must be validated.

EXT-BEACON-NODE-CL.name: Beacon Node via Validator Client API
EXT-BEACON-NODE-CL.entry_point: Validator Client API (signing requests, duty assignments, chain state)
EXT-BEACON-NODE-CL.rationale: Validator client MUST treat the beacon node as potentially compromised. Signing requests must be checked against slashing protection DB. Covers EXT-BEACON-NODE, EXT-BEACON-NODE-UNTRUSTED.

EXT-P2P-GOSSIP-CL.name: CL P2P Gossip Network
EXT-P2P-GOSSIP-CL.rationale: Network peers are unauthenticated. Attestations and aggregates from gossip must be fully validated.

EXT-ETH1-CHAIN.name: ETH1 Chain via Deposit Contract
EXT-ETH1-CHAIN.entry_point: ETH1 deposit data and block hashes for ETH1 voting
EXT-ETH1-CHAIN.rationale: ETH1 data is sourced from an external chain. Merkle proofs for deposits must be verified. A compromised ETH1 endpoint could feed invalid deposit data.

EXT-LIGHT-CLIENT-CL.name: Light Client via LC Protocol
EXT-LIGHT-CLIENT-CL.rationale: Light clients request data from full nodes. From the full node's perspective, serving light clients is a resource expenditure; requests must be rate-limited. From the light client's perspective, all data from full nodes must be verified via Merkle proofs and sync committee signatures.

EXT-GENESIS-SERVER.name: Genesis Config Server via HTTPS
EXT-GENESIS-SERVER.entry_point: HTTP(S) fetch of genesis.json from yolonet.xyz
EXT-GENESIS-SERVER.rationale: External web server. No authentication or integrity verification specified. Compromised server could feed malicious genesis config.

EXT-EF-BOOTNODE.name: EF Bootnode via devp2p
EXT-EF-BOOTNODE.entry_point: devp2p enode connection for peer discovery
EXT-EF-BOOTNODE.rationale: Single bootnode is a centralization risk. P2P connections are unauthenticated beyond node ID.

EXT-ETHSTATS-SERVER.name: Ethstats Server via Reporting Protocol
EXT-ETHSTATS-SERVER.rationale: External monitoring service. Node sends data to it; compromised service could be used for fingerprinting or information disclosure.

EXT-TESTNET-DEVELOPER.name: Protocol Developer via Testnet RPC
EXT-TESTNET-DEVELOPER.entry_point: Contract deployment and experimental opcode invocation via testnet RPC
EXT-TESTNET-DEVELOPER.rationale: Developers on ephemeral testnet submit experimental contract bytecode. No authentication; testnet is permissionless.

EXT-NODE-OPERATOR.name: Node Operator via Configuration
EXT-NODE-OPERATOR.entry_point: Client configuration (weak subjectivity checkpoint, CLI flags)
EXT-NODE-OPERATOR.rationale: Node operators provide initial configuration including weak subjectivity checkpoints. They have local access to the node, which provides some trust basis, but checkpoint data must still be validated against known chain state. A compromised checkpoint enables long-range attacks.

EXT-DAPP-BROWSER.name: Web DApp via Browser RPC
EXT-DAPP-BROWSER.rationale: Web applications communicate with Ethereum nodes via browser-based RPC (EIP-107). DApps can submit arbitrary transaction parameters and RPC method names. The authorization popup mechanism provides user consent but the DApp itself is untrusted. Read-only RPC via iframe is filtered by a whitelist of 43 methods.

EXT-END-USER-UI.name: End User via Authorization UI
EXT-END-USER-UI.rationale: Human users authorize transactions via popup UI. Users may be deceived by UI spoofing attacks, phishing, or social engineering. The user's decision (approve/reject) is trusted as an intent signal but the user cannot be trusted to verify all transaction details correctly.

EXT-DELEGATED-USER-ACCOUNT.name: Delegated User Account via EIP-7702
EXT-DELEGATED-USER-ACCOUNT.entry_point: EIP-7880 EXTCODEADDRESS opcode / EIP-7702 delegation designation
EXT-DELEGATED-USER-ACCOUNT.rationale: Accounts with EIP-7702 delegation designations interact with sponsorship contracts. The delegation status can change between transactions, creating race condition risks. The delegated-to address must be verified via EXTCODEADDRESS before trusting the delegation.

EXT-EL-REQUEST-PRODUCER.name: EL Request Producer (Smart Contracts)
EXT-EL-REQUEST-PRODUCER.rationale: Smart contracts on the EL generate requests (via system contracts or events) that flow to the CL for processing. These requests are committed via SHA256 hash in block headers. The CL must validate all request contents independently as the generating contracts are untrusted.

EXT-DAPP-JSON-RPC.name: DApp via JSON-RPC (EIP-2566)
EXT-DAPP-JSON-RPC.rationale: DApp provides ABI metadata alongside transaction data. ABI is untrusted and may be spoofed to mislead wallet users. Function selector collision attacks are possible.

EXT-WALLET-SIGNER.name: Wallet/Signer via JSON-RPC
EXT-WALLET-SIGNER.rationale: External wallet software that signs transactions with EIP-155 chain ID protection. The signed transaction data entering the EL is untrusted and requires full validation including chain ID verification and signature recovery.

EXT-TX-BROADCASTER-P2P.name: Transaction Broadcaster via P2P
EXT-TX-BROADCASTER-P2P.rationale: Remote peers broadcasting signed transactions over the P2P network. Includes potential replay attack vectors (EIP-155). All received transactions require full validation: signature, chain ID, nonce, balance, fee checks.

EXT-PEER-NODE-CL-P2P.name: Peer Node via CL P2P (gossipsub)
EXT-PEER-NODE-CL-P2P.rationale: Remote CL peers communicating via gossipsub with fork-digest-scoped topics. Relevant for EIP-6800 (Verkle fork version), EIP-7892 (BPO fork digest rotation), and Fulu fork transitions. Peers may advertise incompatible fork digests, attempt eclipse attacks during fork transitions, or send invalid messages.

EXT-TX-SENDER-RPC.name: Transaction Sender via JSON-RPC
EXT-TX-SENDER-RPC.rationale: Unauthenticated user submitting transactions (including access list txs and blob txs). Consolidates EXT-TX-SENDER and EXT-BLOB-TX-SUBMITTER.

EXT-TOKEN-HOLDER-TX.name: DAO Token Holder via Transaction
EXT-TOKEN-HOLDER-TX.entry_point: withdraw() function call on WithdrawDAO recovery contract
EXT-TOKEN-HOLDER-TX.rationale: External user calling contract function. Balance verification is required before fund transfer.

EXT-VALIDATOR-P2P.name: Validator via P2P Gossip
EXT-VALIDATOR-P2P.entry_point: P2P gossip (attestation, beacon block proposal topics)
EXT-VALIDATOR-P2P.rationale: Validators submit attestations and blocks over unauthenticated P2P. Attestation committee_bits, aggregation_bits, and BLS signatures must all be validated. Malicious validators may submit conflicting attestations.

EXT-PROVER-VALIDATOR.name: Execution Proof Prover via P2P
EXT-PROVER-VALIDATOR.rationale: Active validators submitting execution proofs. Must verify: prover is active validator, BLS signature valid (DOMAIN_EXECUTION_PROOF 0x0D000000), proof cryptographically valid via ProofEngine. Proof size capped at MAX_PROOF_SIZE (300 KiB).

EXT-PROOF-CONSUMER-LIGHT-CLIENT.name: Light Client Proof Consumer
EXT-PROOF-CONSUMER-LIGHT-CLIENT.entry_point: Merkle proof requests (EIP-7916 progressive list proofs)
EXT-PROOF-CONSUMER-LIGHT-CLIENT.rationale: Light clients request merkle proofs for list elements. Requests are unauthenticated. Progressive tree gindex computation must be correct to prevent proof forgery.

EXT-KEY-ENCAPSULATION-PEER.name: Key Encapsulation Peer (Sender/Recipient App)
EXT-KEY-ENCAPSULATION-PEER.rationale: Wallet applications exchanging private keys via ECIES. Recipient public key may lack signature verification (optional signerPubKey). Man-in-the-middle possible without trust chain validation. Consolidates EXT-SENDER-APP, EXT-RECIPIENT-APP, EXT-KEY-PROVIDER, EXT-KEY-HOLDER.

EXT-WITHDRAWAL-CREDENTIAL-OWNER-RPC.name: Withdrawal Credential Owner via JSON-RPC
EXT-WITHDRAWAL-CREDENTIAL-OWNER-RPC.rationale: Withdrawal credential holders submit requests via standard transactions. Authorization is verified on CL side by checking source_address against withdrawal credentials, but EL must treat all callers as untrusted. Covers EXT-WITHDRAWAL-CREDENTIAL-OWNER, EXT-CALLER.

EXT-DATA-PROVIDER-OUT-OF-BAND.name: External Historical Data Provider via Out-of-Band
EXT-DATA-PROVIDER-OUT-OF-BAND.entry_point: Out-of-band data retrieval (IPFS, Portal Network, The Graph, torrent)
EXT-DATA-PROVIDER-OUT-OF-BAND.rationale: External data providers supply historical blockchain data after EIP-4444 pruning. Data is retrieved over unauthenticated channels and must be validated against known state roots. Covers EXT-DATA-PROVIDER.

EXT-PROOF-ENGINE-BEACON-API.name: External Proof Engine via Beacon API
EXT-PROOF-ENGINE-BEACON-API.rationale: Proof engines deliver execution proofs asynchronously via the Beacon API. The API endpoint should be access-controlled, providing an authentication basis, but proof content must be cryptographically verified. A compromised proof engine could submit forged proofs. Covers EXT-PROOF-ENGINE, EXT-BEACON-API-CLIENT, EXT-PROVER.

EXT-MINER-BLOCK-PRODUCER.name: Block Producer (Miner) via P2P
EXT-MINER-BLOCK-PRODUCER.entry_point: P2P network (block propagation with difficulty header)
EXT-MINER-BLOCK-PRODUCER.rationale: Miners produce blocks with difficulty values that must be independently validated. A malicious miner could submit blocks with incorrect difficulty. Pre-merge only (EIP-5133). Covered by EXT-MINER.

EXT-SSZ-DATA-SOURCE.name: Serialized Data Source via P2P/Network
EXT-SSZ-DATA-SOURCE.entry_point: P2P network or API (SSZ-encoded container bytes)
EXT-SSZ-DATA-SOURCE.rationale: SSZ-encoded progressive containers (EIP-7495) received from network sources must be fully validated including schema validation, field count checks, and Merkle proof verification. Covers EXT-DATA-SOURCE.

EXT-LIGHT-CLIENT-VERIFIER.name: Light Client / Smart Contract Verifier
EXT-LIGHT-CLIENT-VERIFIER.entry_point: Merkle proof submission (EIP-7495 progressive container proofs)
EXT-LIGHT-CLIENT-VERIFIER.rationale: Light clients submit Merkle proofs for verification. They are consumers of the proof system, but the proofs they present may come from untrusted sources and require full verification. Covers EXT-LIGHT-CLIENT.

EXT-SYNC-COMMITTEE-PEER-P2P.name: Sync Committee Peer via P2P Gossip
EXT-SYNC-COMMITTEE-PEER-P2P.entry_point: P2P gossip network (sync committee message topic)
EXT-SYNC-COMMITTEE-PEER-P2P.rationale: Sync committee messages arrive via unauthenticated P2P gossip. Any node can broadcast messages claiming to be from sync committee members. Messages must be validated against the current sync committee roster and checked for valid signatures.

EXT-AGGREGATION-PEER-P2P.name: Sync Contribution Aggregator via P2P Gossip
EXT-AGGREGATION-PEER-P2P.rationale: Aggregated sync contributions arrive via unauthenticated P2P. Aggregation proofs and included signatures must be fully validated. Malicious aggregators could submit invalid or partial aggregations.

EXT-VALIDATOR-OPERATOR-VIA-TX.name: Validator Operator via Transaction Submission
EXT-VALIDATOR-OPERATOR-VIA-TX.rationale: Validator operators submit consolidation requests as regular EL transactions. No authentication beyond transaction signature. Request format, fee payment, and queue capacity must all be validated. Potential for queue DoS via spam.

EXT-BLOB-SUBMITTER-RPC.name: Blob Transaction Submitter via JSON-RPC
EXT-BLOB-SUBMITTER-RPC.rationale: Blob transactions require additional validation beyond regular transactions: blob gas limit checks, blob fee validation against blob base fee, versioned hash format validation, and blob data presence verification. Contract creation is prohibited for this type.

EXT-PEER-RLPX-INITIATOR.name: Peer Node via RLPx TCP Handshake
EXT-PEER-RLPX-INITIATOR.rationale: Remote peers initiate RLPx connections with auth packets containing signatures and ephemeral keys. EIP-8 mandates forward-compatible parsing that ignores version mismatches and extra RLP elements. While ECIES encryption authenticates the static key, the peer's identity and intentions are untrusted. Tolerant parsing increases attack surface for malformed packets.

EXT-REMOTE-PEER-HELLO.name: Remote Peer via devp2p Hello
EXT-REMOTE-PEER-HELLO.rationale: After RLPx handshake, peers exchange Hello packets with capability advertisements. EIP-8 tolerant parsing ignores version mismatches. Malicious peers could advertise false capabilities or exploit tolerant parsing.

EXT-DISCOVERY-PEER-UDP.name: Discovery Peer via UDP
EXT-DISCOVERY-PEER-UDP.rationale: UDP discovery packets are unauthenticated and spoofable. EIP-8 mandates tolerant parsing with 1280-byte size limit. Unknown packet types are silently discarded. Eclipse attacks possible via discovery manipulation.

EXT-TX-SIGNER-WALLET.name: Transaction Signer via Wallet
EXT-TX-SIGNER-WALLET.rationale: Users or wallets construct and sign transactions. EIP-2718 requires type byte inclusion in signed data for domain separation. If signing is implemented incorrectly (omitting type byte), cross-type signature reuse attacks become possible. The signer is external to the validation node.

EXT-USER-DAPP-TYPE1.name: User/dApp Submitting Type 1 Transaction
EXT-USER-DAPP-TYPE1.rationale: Users or dApps submit Type 1 (EIP-2930) transactions that wallets must automatically convert to Type 2 (EIP-1559). The conversion must preserve transaction intent. Incorrect gas_price to max_fee mapping could result in unexpected fee economics.

EXT-FULL-NODE-P2P.name: Full Node via P2P Network (Light Client Server)
EXT-FULL-NODE-P2P.entry_point: P2P gossip / Beacon API light client endpoints
EXT-FULL-NODE-P2P.rationale: Full nodes providing light client updates, bootstraps, and headers are untrusted peers on the P2P network. Any node can serve fabricated data. The light client protocol relies on cryptographic verification (BLS aggregate signatures, Merkle proofs) to validate data from these untrusted sources.

EXT-UNTRUSTED-LC-SERVER.name: Untrusted Light Client Server
EXT-UNTRUSTED-LC-SERVER.entry_point: P2P gossip / Beacon API (LightClientUpdate, LightClientFinalityUpdate, LightClientBootstrap)
EXT-UNTRUSTED-LC-SERVER.rationale: Any node providing light client data may be malicious or compromised. All received updates must be cryptographically verified including sync committee signatures, finality Merkle proofs, and execution payload proofs (Capella+).

EXT-USER-TRUST-SOURCE.name: External Trust Source (Out-of-Band Bootstrap)
EXT-USER-TRUST-SOURCE.entry_point: Out-of-band mechanism (social consensus, trusted website) providing initial trusted block root
EXT-USER-TRUST-SOURCE.rationale: The initial trusted block root is obtained through external, unverifiable means. If compromised, the entire light client chain of trust collapses. Treated as UNTRUSTED because there is no cryptographic authentication of this channel.

EXT-EXECUTION-ENGINE.name: Execution Engine via Engine API
EXT-EXECUTION-ENGINE.rationale: The execution engine is a locally co-deployed component communicating via authenticated Engine API (JWT). It is trusted for correct execution of state transitions and Verkle proof verification. However, a buggy or compromised EL could return incorrect results, so it is SEMI_TRUSTED.

EXT-P2P-PEERS-DAS.name: P2P Peers (Data Availability Sampling)
EXT-P2P-PEERS-DAS.rationale: Peers providing column sidecar data for data availability are untrusted. They may withhold data, serve invalid columns, or misrepresent custody capabilities in their ENR. Column data must be verified against KZG commitments.

EXT-MALICIOUS-VALIDATOR.name: Malicious Validator via P2P (Archetypal)
EXT-MALICIOUS-VALIDATOR.rationale: Archetypal attack vector: a malicious validator can propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations (triggering slashing conditions), or attempt censorship. All validator-sourced data must be validated against consensus rules.

EXT-VALIDATOR-PROPOSER-P2P.name: Block Proposer via P2P Gossip
EXT-VALIDATOR-PROPOSER-P2P.rationale: Block proposers submit signed beacon blocks via P2P gossip. Any validator can propose, and proposals may be malicious (invalid blocks, equivocating proposals). Data is unauthenticated at the network level; signature verification is part of the processing. Covers EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER and EXT-PROPOSER from the Gloas fork choice subgraphs.

EXT-PTC-VALIDATOR-P2P.name: PTC Committee Validator via P2P Gossip
