EXT-PTC-VALIDATOR-P2P.rationale: PTC validators submit payload timeliness attestations via gossip. A colluding majority (>256 of 512) could manipulate fork choice between FULL and EMPTY tracks. Individual attestations cannot be trusted without committee-level threshold verification.

EXT-RPC-PROVIDER-UNTRUSTED.name: Untrusted RPC Provider
EXT-RPC-PROVIDER-UNTRUSTED.rationale: From a light client or verifier perspective, the RPC provider returning proof data or gas cap info is untrusted. Proof data must be cryptographically verified against a trusted stateRoot. Covers EXT-RPC-PROVIDER and EXT-RPC-NODE.

EXT-EVM-CALLER-CONTRACT.name: Smart Contract via EVM CALL
EXT-EVM-CALLER-CONTRACT.entry_point: EVM CALL opcode to precompiles (address 0x8 for bn128 pairing)
EXT-EVM-CALLER-CONTRACT.rationale: Any smart contract can call precompiles with arbitrary input data. Input must be rigorously validated (length, point encoding, subgroup membership). Covers EXT-EVM-CALLER.

EXT-CONSENSUS-LAYER-LIGHT-CLIENT.name: Consensus Layer / Light Client Sync
EXT-CONSENSUS-LAYER-LIGHT-CLIENT.entry_point: Beacon chain sync / light client protocol (trusted block headers)
EXT-CONSENSUS-LAYER-LIGHT-CLIENT.rationale: Provides trusted block headers used as trust anchors for Merkle proof verification. The consensus mechanism provides cryptoeconomic guarantees but is not infallible. Covers EXT-CONSENSUS-LAYER from EIP-1186.

EXT-STAKER-VIA-DEPOSIT-TX.name: Staker via Deposit Transaction
EXT-STAKER-VIA-DEPOSIT-TX.rationale: Any user can submit deposit transactions. Deposit data (pubkey, withdrawal_credentials, signature) is attacker-controlled and must be fully validated. Derived from EXT-STAKER in spec_bcbc93ac.

EXT-DEPOSIT-ATTACKER.name: DoS Attacker via Deposit Spam
EXT-DEPOSIT-ATTACKER.entry_point: Deposit contract calls (mass deposit submission for DoS)
EXT-DEPOSIT-ATTACKER.rationale: Attacker submitting maximum deposits per block to slow processing. Cost ~1000 ETH to delay by 1 second makes it economically difficult but not impossible. Derived from EXT-ATTACKER in spec_bcbc93ac.

EXT-NEW-VALIDATOR-DEPOSIT-CL.name: New Validator Deposit via Beacon Chain
EXT-NEW-VALIDATOR-DEPOSIT-CL.entry_point: Validator deposit processing (index allocation in EIP-6914)
EXT-NEW-VALIDATOR-DEPOSIT-CL.rationale: Deposits originate from EL and are processed by CL. The timing and targeting of deposits could be manipulated to exploit index reuse. Derived from EXT-NEW-VALIDATOR-DEPOSIT in spec_ae8092dc.

EXT-FULL-NODE-LC-PUBLISHER.name: Full Node via Light Client Gossip
EXT-FULL-NODE-LC-PUBLISHER.rationale: Full nodes publish light client updates over gossip. Light clients cannot fully trust any single publisher; updates must be validated via sync committee signatures. Derived from EXT-FULL-NODE in spec_b2c6a56e.

EXT-SERVING-PEER-LC-REQRESP.name: Serving Peer via Light Client Req/Resp
EXT-SERVING-PEER-LC-REQRESP.entry_point: GetLightClientBootstrap, LightClientUpdatesByRange, GetLightClientFinalityUpdate, GetLightClientOptimisticUpdate req/resp protocols
EXT-SERVING-PEER-LC-REQRESP.rationale: Serving peers respond to light client queries. Responses contain fork-versioned SSZ data that must be validated before processing. Derived from EXT-SERVING-PEER in spec_b2c6a56e.

EXT-UNTRUSTED-PEER-SSZ.name: Untrusted Peer via SSZ Messages
EXT-UNTRUSTED-PEER-SSZ.entry_point: P2P network SSZ-encoded light client messages
EXT-UNTRUSTED-PEER-SSZ.rationale: Any peer can send SSZ-encoded messages. Fork version must be validated before deserialization to prevent type confusion attacks. Derived from EXT-UNTRUSTED-PEER in spec_b2c6a56e.

EXT-WS-CHECKPOINT-PROVIDER.name: Weak Subjectivity Checkpoint Provider
EXT-WS-CHECKPOINT-PROVIDER.entry_point: Checkpoint sync endpoint (external API providing ws_state and ws_checkpoint)
EXT-WS-CHECKPOINT-PROVIDER.rationale: Checkpoint providers are semi-trusted: they are explicitly chosen by the node operator and represent community consensus. However, a compromised provider could direct nodes onto an attacker-controlled fork. Derived from EXT-CHECKPOINT-PROVIDER in spec_b7dca68c.

EXT-MALICIOUS-VALIDATOR-EB-GRIND.name: Malicious Validator via Effective Balance Grinding
EXT-MALICIOUS-VALIDATOR-EB-GRIND.entry_point: Beacon chain validator operations (balance adjustments, RANDAO observation)
EXT-MALICIOUS-VALIDATOR-EB-GRIND.rationale: Validator attempting to manipulate effective balance after observing RANDAO to influence proposer selection. EIP-7917 lookahead mechanism defends against this. Derived from EXT-MALICIOUS-VALIDATOR in spec_bff057a3.

EXT-BEACON-NETWORK-RANDAO.name: Beacon Network (RANDAO Reveals)
EXT-BEACON-NETWORK-RANDAO.rationale: RANDAO values are publicly revealed in block proposals. Any validator can observe them. The security relies on unpredictability at the time effective balances are set, not on secrecy. Derived from EXT-NETWORK in spec_bff057a3.

EXT-BLS-SIGNATURE-SOURCE.name: BLS Signature Source via P2P Gossip
EXT-BLS-SIGNATURE-SOURCE.entry_point: Aggregate signatures received via P2P gossip (attestations, sync committee messages)
EXT-BLS-SIGNATURE-SOURCE.rationale: Aggregate signatures and public keys arrive from P2P network peers. Any validator or peer can submit signatures; they must be cryptographically verified via FastAggregateVerify. The empty-set edge case (G2 point at infinity) is a critical validation boundary.

EXT-DEPOSITOR-CL.name: New Validator Depositor via Beacon Chain
EXT-DEPOSITOR-CL.entry_point: Validator deposit processing (index reuse in EIP-6914)
EXT-DEPOSITOR-CL.rationale: Depositors trigger index allocation. An attacker could attempt to target specific reused indices. The SAFE_EPOCHS_TO_REUSE_INDEX time-lock (65536 epochs, ~0.8 years) is the primary defense. Derived from EXT-DEPOSITOR in spec_ca22aab3.

EXT-HISTORICAL-INDEX-REFERENCES.name: Historical Index References (External Systems)
EXT-HISTORICAL-INDEX-REFERENCES.entry_point: External API queries referencing validator indices
EXT-HISTORICAL-INDEX-REFERENCES.rationale: Block explorers, staking dashboards, and indexers reference validator indices by number. After index reuse, identity changes could cause confusion. These systems must handle identity changes. Derived from EXT-HISTORICAL-REFERENCES in spec_ca22aab3.

EXT-EVM-CALLER-MODEXP.name: Smart Contract Caller via ModExp Precompile
EXT-EVM-CALLER-MODEXP.rationale: Any smart contract can call the ModExp precompile with arbitrary input. The gas formula must accurately price computation to prevent DoS. EIP-7883 increases costs 150-9105% to better reflect actual compute. Derived from EXT-EVM-CALLER in spec_ce43b11f.

EXT-WHISK-BLOCK-PROPOSER.name: Block Proposer via P2P (Whisk SSLE)
EXT-WHISK-BLOCK-PROPOSER.entry_point: Beacon block with Whisk shuffle proof, opening proof, and tracker data
EXT-WHISK-BLOCK-PROPOSER.rationale: Block proposers submit ZK proofs (Curdleproofs shuffle ~32KB, opening ~1KB) that must be validated. Invalid proofs must cause block rejection. A malicious proposer could try to forge proofs to hijack future slots. Derived from EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER and EXT-ANONYMOUS-PROPOSER in spec_d0b2f2d8.

EXT-ETH66-PEER-NODE.name: Remote Peer via eth/66 Protocol
EXT-ETH66-PEER-NODE.entry_point: eth/66 P2P request-response messages with request_id correlation
EXT-ETH66-PEER-NODE.rationale: Remote peers send eth/66 protocol messages with request IDs. Malicious peers could send incorrect request_ids, forge responses, or attempt request flooding. RLP message structure must be validated. Derived from EXT-PEER-NODE in spec_d30530f6.

EXT-LC-NETWORK-PEER-FORK.name: Network Peer via Light Client Protocol (Cross-Fork)
EXT-LC-NETWORK-PEER-FORK.entry_point: P2P light client data in pre-Capella or current format
EXT-LC-NETWORK-PEER-FORK.rationale: Peers may send light client data in older fork formats. Local conversion must handle malformed data safely. Empty ExecutionPayloadHeader defaults must not pass as valid execution proofs. Derived from EXT-NETWORK-PEER in spec_d4463816.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_005b84bce6ddb.target_component_interface: devp2p eth/70 Block Data Request Handler
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_005b84bce6ddb.security_assumption: All incoming P2P requests must be validated for block number range (>= 15,537,393 for post-PoS). Pre-PoS data requests must be rejected. Message format must be validated against eth/70 protocol spec.
Block number scope validation required. Must reject requests targeting blocks below Paris upgrade boundary. Rate limiting on request volume to prevent resource exhaustion.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_005b84bce6ddb.target_component_interface: Block validation pipeline (difficulty, reward, fork activation)
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_005b84bce6ddb.security_assumption: Full block header validation required: difficulty must match computed expected difficulty using EIP-649 rules (fake block number with 3M offset for post-Byzantium). Block reward must be exactly 3 ETH (post-Byzantium). Fork activation block numbers must be checked.

EIP-150 gas repricing must be applied for all IO-heavy operations (SLOAD, BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, CALL, etc.) at post-Tangerine Whistle blocks (>= 2,463,000). Gas costs must accurately reflect computational cost to prevent DoS.

The checkpoint root must be verified against a trusted source (weak subjectivity assumption). The bootstrap object returned must be cryptographically verified against the checkpoint root. No authentication of the provider itself is possible.

All updates must be validated against sync committee signatures. At least 2/3 supermajority of sync committee signatures required. Finalized header advancement must be verified. Fork version transitions must be handled correctly.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_005b84bce6ddb.target_component_interface: Light client P2P req/resp (bootstrap, updates by range)
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_005b84bce6ddb.security_assumption: Responses from peers must be cryptographically verified. Multiple peers should be queried to prevent eclipse attacks. Connection to at least one honest full node assumed.
Must validate: (1) current_epoch >= CAPELLA_FORK_EPOCH, (2) first valid change per validator index, (3) full process_bls_to_execution_change validation. Reject/ignore messages failing any check.
Fork digest must match expected Capella fork digest. Block contents including embedded bls_to_execution_changes must be fully validated.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_005b84bce6ddb.target_component_interface: BeaconBlocksByRange v2 / BeaconBlocksByRoot v2 response handler
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_005b84bce6ddb.security_assumption: Fork version must be correctly determined via compute_fork_version for each block's epoch. outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_5c0663ff1d6c..security_assumption: All light client headers must pass: (1) blob gas field validation for pre-Deneb epochs (must be zero), (2) execution payload emptiness check for pre-Capella epochs, (3) Merkle branch verification of execution root against beacon body root. Headers from any source are fully untrusted.

Block header excess_blob_gas must exactly match calc_excess_blob_gas computation with timestamp-based fork boundary reset. Mismatch must result in block rejection. Special attention needed at fork boundary where excess_blob_gas resets to 0.

Input must be exactly 213 bytes. Final flag byte must be exactly 0 or 1. Gas cost = rounds * 1 must be available. High rounds values (up to 2^32-1) are valid but gas-metered. All input fields (h, m, t, f) are attacker-controlled and must produce deterministic RFC 7693 output.

The block_access_list_root provided by EL must be validated by CL. At fork transition it is initialized to Root() (zero). Post-fork, CL must verify EL-provided values are consistent with execution payload content.

JWT authentication required. ForkchoiceState must be validated: headBlockHash must reference a known valid payload, safeBlockHash must be ancestor of head, finalizedBlockHash must be consistent. Payload attributes must have valid timestamp. Message ordering must be enforced sequentially.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_5c0663ff1d6c..target_component_interface: Engine API JWT authentication on port 8551
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_5c0663ff1d6c..security_assumption: All requests must present a valid JWT bearer token signed with the shared secret. Invalid or missing JWT must result in immediate rejection. The shared secret must be securely generated and stored. Communication should occur over localhost or trusted network.

DApp-provided ABIs are untrusted. Wallets must: (1) validate interface spec version, (2) perform case-sensitive address matching, (3) optionally verify against trusted ABI database, (4) clearly indicate to users when ABI source is unverified. Decoded calldata display must not be presented as authoritative.

Wallets must assume all DApp-provided ABIs could be misleading. Users must be warned that decoded transaction details are only as trustworthy as the providing DApp. Wallets should indicate verified vs. unverified ABI sources visually.

User approval drives transaction signing. Wallet must present accurate information about trust level of decoded data. Users may be misled by malicious ABIs; wallet UI must distinguish verified from unverified decoded calldata.

Database responses are delivered over HTTPS. Database may not have entries for all contracts. Absence of verification does not imply malicious intent. Wallet must handle missing entries gracefully and indicate unverified status to user.

Full validation pipeline required: (1) correct subnet routing (column_index % SUBNET_COUNT == subnet_id), (2) temporal bounds (not future, within finalized range), (3) proposer signature verification, (4) KZG commitments inclusion Merkle proof, (5) batch KZG proof verification, (6) proposer index matches expected shuffling. REJECT for cryptographic failures, IGNORE for timing issues.

Request parameters must be validated: start_slot and count within data_column_serve_range, request size within MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB limits, block_root since minimum_request_epoch. Oversized requests must be rejected. Resource unavailability (code 3) returned for data outside serve range.

Input must contain only valid hex characters (0-9, a-f, A-F) after optional 0x prefix. Fixed-size outputs enforce exact byte lengths via padding. Type wrappers (U8, U64, U256) must enforce bounds checking. Invalid input must raise handled exceptions, not crash the node.

Mining clients should validate epoch parameters, target difficulty values, extranonce bounds (max 6 bytes), and header hash format. Stale job indicators must be honored.

All messages must pass: JSON format validation (LF terminated), message type classification (request/response/notification), hex format validation (lowercase, no 0x prefix, minimal digits). Invalid messages return error codes: 2xx conditional, 3xx auth, 4xx syntax, 5xx server.

ENR validation: size <= 300 bytes, valid RLP, sorted unique keys, valid secp256k1 signature over keccak256 of content. Sequence number must be checked for freshness. Unknown identity schemes must be rejected.

Domain separator prevents cross-contract and cross-chain replay. Same-domain replay prevention requires application-level nonce tracking. Verifying contracts must correctly implement EIP-712 encoding and check domain separator fields.

JWT-authenticated channel. EL must produce execution payloads that include exactly the specified withdrawals. Content validation: withdrawal amounts, validator indices, and execution addresses must match CL state. A malicious CL could specify incorrect withdrawals.

Pre-fork (Deneb) format data must be locally upgraded to Electra format using upgrade functions. Merkle branches must be normalized using Electra generalized indices. All cryptographic verification (sync committee signatures) must pass after format conversion.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_5c62ef3303650.target_component_interface: Transaction Pool (access list processing, Amsterdam fork)
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_5c62ef3303650.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required including access list structure, gas pricing for warm/cold slots, and intrinsic gas calculation. Malformed access lists must be rejected.
Identity precompile performs no input validation by design—gas cost must scale with input size to prevent resource amplification. Output is untrusted pass-through data.

Input signature parameters (v, r, s) must be validated: v must be 27 or 28, r and s must be in range (0, SECP256K1N). Invalid inputs must return empty output without reverting. Cryptographic library must be correctly implemented.

Gas cost must be calculated before execution using EIP-2565 formula: max(200, floor(complexity * iteration_count / 3)). Input lengths parsed from calldata must be validated. Minimum gas floor of 200 prevents spam.
Minimum gas floor of 200 must be enforced. Gas formula must accurately reflect actual computation cost across all client implementations to prevent underpricing attacks.

Full block structure validation required: header conformance to fork rules, state trie updates, bloom filter computation, and transaction execution. Invalid blocks must be rejected without state corruption.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_5c62ef3303650.target_component_interface: Weak Subjectivity Checkpoint Validation (CLI startup parameter)
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_5c62ef3303650.security_assumption: Checkpoint format must be parsed and validated: block root must match canonical chain at specified epoch. If checkpoint epoch > finalized epoch, block must exist in canonical chain. If checkpoint epoch <= finalized epoch, root must match. Invalid checkpoints must cause client termination with descriptive error.

Conflicting finalized checkpoints require at least 1/3 of total stake to be slashable. WS checkpoint must reject attacker forks. Safety margin of at least 1/3 - SAFETY_DECAY/100 (~23.3%) must be maintained within the WS period.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_5c62ef3303650.target_component_interface: PeerDAS Data Column Sidecar Gossip Verification
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_5c62ef3303650.security_assumption: Each data column sidecar must pass: (1) batched KZG commitment verification, (2) inclusion proof verification. Invalid columns must be rejected and validation failures tracked via metrics. Reconstruction of missing columns must only use verified data.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_d4cf94fc18efc.security_assumption: Full request validation required: rate limiting for eth_config (recommended 1s interval), transaction format validation, authorization tuple validation for type-4 transactions. Access should be restricted to trusted interfaces where possible.
Rate limiting must be enforced to prevent DDoS. Endpoint access should be restricted to trusted interfaces only. Configuration data exposure is an information leak risk.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_d4cf94fc18efc.target_component_interface: P2P gossip blob_sidecar_{subnet_id} and beacon_block topics
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_d4cf94fc18efc.security_assumption: Full cryptographic validation required: blob index < MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK, correct subnet mapping, valid proposer signature, valid Merkle inclusion proof, valid KZG proof, blob_kzg_commitments count <= MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK.
Enforce MAX_REQUEST_BLOB_SIDECARS (768) limit. Verify requested slots are within MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS retention window. Return ResourceUnavailable error for out-of-window requests.

Bootstrap must be verified against trusted block root (out-of-band). Updates require valid sync committee aggregate signatures (>= 2/3 threshold). Finality updates must contain valid finality proof. Light client must verify all data cryptographically before accepting.
Configuration data from any single node must be cross-checked against multiple sources and the official specification. Never trust a single node's configuration response for fork readiness decisions.

STATICCALL (EIP-214) enforces read-only execution: CREATE, LOG, SSTORE, SELFDESTRUCT, CALL-with-value are prohibited. STATIC flag must propagate correctly through nested calls. For EIP-7702 delegated EOAs, delegation resolves only one level. Precompile inputs (EIP-1108) must be validated: point-on-curve check, input length validation.

Type-4 transaction validation: non-empty authorization list, non-null destination, sender must be EOA or delegated. Each authorization: chain_id must be 0 or current, nonce < 2^64-1, valid ecrecover with MAGIC prefix, s <= secp256k1n/2, authority code empty or existing delegation, authority nonce matches.

Nonce-based replay protection: authority nonce is incremented after each successful authorization, so replayed tuples will fail nonce match. Cross-chain replay is possible if chain_id=0 was used in the original authorization.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_d88b3f9b541e..target_component_interface: e2store / Portal Network / EIP-7801 data retrieval
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_d88b3f9b541e..security_assumption: All externally sourced historical data must be validated against known canonical block hashes, transaction roots, and receipt roots. Data integrity verification is mandatory before serving to RPC clients.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_014c3d8c3b4c..security_assumption: All received transactions must be fully validated (signature, nonce, gas, initcode size per EIP-3860). Blob transactions received without sidecars must not be forwarded until all blobs are fetched and validated (EIP-8094).

Blob data received via PooledBlobs must have hash correspondence validated against requested vhashes. Missing or mismatched blobs must be handled gracefully. Nodes MUST NOT forward transactions with unvalidated blobs.

All P2P messages must use correct fork version encoding (EIP-7928). Messages with incorrect fork versions must be rejected. Fork version is determined by epoch threshold checks in strict descending order.

Full transaction validation required: signature verification, chain ID check (EIP-155 replay protection), initcode size <= 49152 bytes for creation transactions (EIP-3860), gas limit >= intrinsic gas including initcode cost, contract code size <= 24KB (EIP-170).

CL relies on EL to correctly execute and validate payloads. The Engine API channel is JWT-authenticated. CL still validates parent_hash consistency, RANDAO, timestamp, and no-empty-transactions constraint independently before delegating full execution validation to EL (Bellatrix).

EL must validate execution payload content (transaction validity, state transitions, gas accounting) regardless of CL authentication. JWT authentication ensures channel integrity but not content correctness.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_014c3d8c3b4c..target_component_interface: Beacon block proposal via P2P gossip
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_014c3d8c3b4c..security_assumption: Proposed blocks must pass full validation: execution payload checks (parent hash, RANDAO, timestamp), signature verification, slot/epoch consistency. Equivocating proposers must be slashed.

Relay is expected to return valid, highest-value bids and reveal full payloads after proposer commitment. Proposer should implement fallback to local block building if relay is unresponsive. Relay failure after signing results in missed slot (liveness risk).
Builder payloads must be validated by the relay before being presented to proposers. Invalid payloads, censored blocks, or undervalued bids should be filtered by relay validation.
Searcher bundles are untrusted transaction orderings. Standard transaction validation applies to all individual transactions within bundles.

Slashing evidence must be cryptographically verified (conflicting signatures from same validator). Reporter identity is irrelevant — evidence validity is independently verifiable. Bellatrix parameters: MIN_SLASHING_PENALTY_QUOTIENT=32, PROPORTIONAL_SLASHING_MULTIPLIER=3.

Input must be exactly 160 bytes. Signature bounds (0 < r,s < n), public key field bounds (0 <= qx,qy < p), curve equation membership, and non-identity point checks are all required. Gas (6900) is consumed regardless of validation outcome. Signatures are malleable (both (r,s) and (r,n-s) valid) per EIP-7951.

Blocks must be validated against fork-specific rules. At block 2,675,000 (Spurious Dragon), EIP-155 replay protection, EIP-160 EXP cost, EIP-161 state clearing, and EIP-170 code size limits activate. All blocks must meet applicable rule set.

Historical state must be available for the requested block.

Object-format parameters must not contain both blockNumber and blockHash simultaneously. Parameter type detection must handle all three formats (hex, tag, object) without ambiguity. Invalid formats must return appropriate JSON-RPC errors.

Peer status must be validated: networkid, genesis hash, and forkid must match. Incompatible peers must be disconnected. The earliestBlock and latestBlock values are self-reported and cannot be trusted until verified by actual block requests.

Block range updates are rate-limited (max once per epoch/32 blocks). Range claims must be treated as unverified. Peers failing to serve blocks within claimed ranges should be penalized via peer scoring. No more than one update per epoch should be accepted.

Receipts in eth/69 format omit bloom filters. Receiving nodes must recompute bloom filters from logs if needed for local queries. Receipt data must be validated against expected block hashes. The compact format [tx-type, post-state-or-status, cumulative-gas, logs] must be correctly parsed.

Status message validation: networkid, genesis, forkid must match. blockRange is self-reported and unverified. Peer's claimed range must be stored but not trusted until validated by actual block requests.

Range responses may contain multiple [startBlock, endBlock] tuples representing non-contiguous ranges. Responses must be treated as unverified claims. Dishonest range claims detected via failed block requests should trigger peer scoring penalties. Sybil resistance depends on diverse peer selection.

Blocks must pass consensus-layer validation (slot, proposer, signature, parent) and execution payload timestamp check before propagation. Blocks with invalid execution payloads SHOULD NOT cause peer downscoring (prevents network segregation between optimistic and non-optimistic nodes). Message size up to 10 MiB due to ExecutionPayload.
Responses must use correct fork-version-appropriate SSZ schema (phase0, altair, or bellatrix) for each requested block. Response chunks limited to 10 MiB each. Fork version determined by block slot.

All column sidecars must be structurally verified via verify_data_column_sidecar and cryptographically verified via verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs. Retrieval failure triggers block queuing (not rejection). Data availability is guaranteed only within MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS window.

Blocks must pass sequential validation: parent exists in store, slot is valid, finality constraints met, data availability confirmed via DAS (is_data_available without blob_kzg_commitments). Only after all checks pass is state transition executed. Blocks failing DA check MAY be queued for later processing.

Full PoW validation: difficulty target verification, total difficulty computation against TTD, ethash proof verification. Blocks claiming to reach TTD must be carefully validated to prevent premature or malicious merge triggering.

User approval triggers 3-second account unlock window. Authorization popup must accurately display transaction details. UI spoofing must be prevented by the browser environment.

Blocks must be validated against fork-specific consensus rules. For Muir Glacier (EIP-2387): verify block number >= 9,200,000 triggers EIP-2384 difficulty bomb delay. Difficulty calculation must use correct fake block number offset. All transactions in block must pass all validation rules.

All precompile inputs arrive via transactions from untrusted users. ALT_BN128: validate input length (64/128/192*n bytes), field element < modulus, point on curve, subgroup membership. BLS12-381: validate input length per operation type, field elements < BLS12 modulus, point on curve, subgroup check (point * curve_order == infinity). BLAKE2F: validate input exactly 213 bytes, final flag in {0,1}. Gas must be correctly charged before execution.

All system opcode invocations originate from user transactions. Must validate: init code size <= MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE, address collision checks (EIP-7610 storage collision), call depth <= 1024, sender nonce < 2^64-1, sender balance >= endowment/value, static context restrictions for value transfer and SELFDESTRUCT. EIP-6780: SELFDESTRUCT only deletes contracts created in same transaction.

EXTCODEADDRESS resolves only one level of delegation. Delegation target is NOT warmed (subsequent cold access costs apply). Sponsorship contracts must verify delegation target against whitelist. Delegation can change between transactions (TOCTOU risk).
JWT authentication validates channel but payload content must be validated. Block payloads must pass all EL validation rules. The CL is trusted for fork choice but not for payload correctness.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_61c006644949..security_assumption: All sync committee messages must be validated: (1) sender is in current sync committee, (2) signature is valid over the correct beacon block root, (3) message timing is within acceptable window per SYNC_MESSAGE_DUE_BPS.

Aggregated contributions must be validated: (1) aggregation bits and signatures are consistent, (2) included individual messages are valid, (3) submission timing is within CONTRIBUTION_DUE_BPS window.

Full validation required: (1) source address is 20 bytes, source/target pubkeys are 48 bytes each, (2) fee payment covers computed exponential fee, (3) queue has not exceeded 262,144 capacity limit. Requests exceeding capacity are discarded without refund.

Exit requests must be validated against validator registry. Weight-based churn limiting (256 ETH initial limit) must correctly handle partial exits and deferred processing. Large validator exits (up to 2048 ETH) must not bypass churn limits.

Full transaction validation pipeline: (1) type detection via first byte ([0x00-0x7f] typed, [0xc0-0xfe] legacy), (2) type-specific payload decoding and validation, (3) signature verification with type byte in signed data (domain separation), (4) fee validation (max_fee >= base_fee, priority_fee <= max_fee), (5) nonce and balance checks.

Blob-specific validation required: (1) blob gas within protocol limit, (2) max_fee_per_blob_gas >= current blob base fee, (3) versioned hash has correct 0x01 prefix and 32-byte length with valid KZG correspondence, (4) blob data actually present, (5) contract creation prohibited for Type 3.

Auth packet must be decryptable via ECIES with recipient's static key. Required fields (signature, initiator-pubk, initiator-nonce) must be present. Version mismatches and extra RLP elements are tolerated per EIP-8 but must not cause crashes or buffer overflows. Random padding (100-300 bytes) should use cryptographically secure randomness.

Hello packets parsed with forward-compatible tolerance. Version mismatches ignored. Capability advertisements must not be trusted without further protocol-level validation. Additional list elements and trailing data ignored safely.

Packets must not exceed 1280 bytes. Unknown packet types silently discarded. Known types (ping/pong/findnode/neighbours) processed with tolerant RLP parsing. UDP source addresses are spoofable — no authentication at transport level.

Permission system must: (1) correctly identify invoker origin without spoofing, (2) present clear consent UI resistant to clickjacking, (3) enforce caveat restrictions on method calls, (4) validate URLs against SSRF (scheme and port whitelisting), (5) filter permissions by invoker on query. Error 4001 returned on user rejection per EIP-1193.

Signed data MUST include TransactionType byte as first byte to ensure domain separation per EIP-2718. Signature verification must reject signatures where type byte is missing or mismatched, preventing cross-type signature reuse attacks.

Conversion must correctly map gas_price to both max_fee_per_gas and max_priority_fee_per_gas. Access list must be preserved unchanged. Chain ID must be maintained. Type field updated from 0x1 to 0x2. Incorrect conversion could alter transaction economics.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_781903032afb..target_component_interface: P2P gossip / Beacon API light client endpoints
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_781903032afb..security_assumption: All light client updates must be cryptographically verified: BLS aggregate signature verification over sync committee, Merkle branch verification for finality and execution payload proofs, slot ordering validation, and minimum participation threshold checks.

Full cryptographic verification pipeline required: sync committee signature verification, finality Merkle proof verification, execution payload Merkle proof verification (Capella+). No update should be applied without passing all validation steps.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_781903032afb..target_component_interface: Light client bootstrap initialization (trusted block root input)
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_781903032afb..security_assumption: The trusted block root MUST correspond to a canonical chain block. If this root is compromised, all subsequent light client validation is compromised. This is the root of trust for the entire light client protocol. Users must obtain this via reliable out-of-band channels.

JWT authentication validates the channel. However, execution payload content must be fully validated: parent hash consistency, RANDAO mix, timestamp alignment, blob commitment counts, transaction validity, and (post-EIP-6800) Verkle witness verification. The CL relays proposer data which may be adversarial.

Block proposer data must be validated through complete consensus validation pipeline: slot verification, proposer eligibility, execution payload validity via Engine API, and (post-EIP-6800) Verkle witness structural and cryptographic verification.

The CL trusts the EL to correctly verify execution payloads and return accurate results. JWT authenticates the channel. The CL cannot independently re-verify execution-layer state transitions. A compromised EL would compromise CL's view of execution validity.

All blocks and transactions from P2P peers must be independently validated: block header fields (difficulty, gas limit, timestamp), transaction signatures, nonce ordering, gas pricing, state transition correctness. Eclipse attack mitigations required.

Block difficulty must be independently recalculated using the difficulty formula with fork-adjusted block numbers (post-Muir Glacier: max(0, block.number - 9,000,000)). Stated difficulty in headers cannot be trusted.

Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce validation, gas limit checks, balance sufficiency (or zero-balance handling per EIP-7768), contract code size limits (24KB per EIP-170), and state clearing rules (EIP-161). For EIP-7768 no-ether transactions, proposer must perform double-execution verification to ensure consideration consistency.

Column sidecar data must be verified against KZG commitments from the beacon block. Peers may serve invalid columns or withhold data. Custody group assignments must be independently computed. ENR custody claims cannot be trusted without verification.

All validator messages must be validated against consensus rules. Invalid blocks must be rejected. Conflicting attestations must trigger slashing detection. Proposer eligibility must be verified. No validator message should be trusted based solely on validator identity.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_781903032afb..target_component_interface: MEV-Boost relay API / External builder API
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_781903032afb..security_assumption: Execution payloads from external builders via MEV-Boost relays must be fully validated through the same pipeline as locally-built payloads. No trust should be placed in relay assertions about payload validity or value. Relay availability cannot be guaranteed.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_ada88c29a21d2.security_assumption: EL must independently validate fork activation criteria (block number/timestamp). JWT authentication ensures channel integrity but fork parameters must be verified against local configuration.
Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce check, gas limit validation, balance sufficiency, EIP-2718 type envelope parsing.
Input parameters must be validated to prevent resource exhaustion during estimation. Malformed transaction parameters should be rejected before simulation.
Full block validation required: header validation, transaction execution, state root verification, receipt root verification. Malformed blocks must be rejected without crashing.

Deposit logs must be filtered by exact contract address (0x00000000219ab540356cbb839cbe05303d7705fa) and event signature hash. Data must be exactly 576 bytes. Field parsing is structural; cryptographic validation deferred to CL.

Economic cost of deposit spam (~1000 ETH per second of delay) provides primary defense. Maximum 8192 deposits per payload caps worst-case processing. BLS signature verification timing must be bounded.

Index reuse must atomically clear equivocation history via on_reused_index(). Attacker must not be able to time deposits to receive specific indices. is_reusable_validator() must enforce sufficient cooldown period.
Fork version must be validated before SSZ deserialization. Light client updates must be verified against sync committee signatures. Rate limiting via gossipsub scoring assumed.
Bootstrap data must be validated against known checkpoint. Fork-versioned SSZ type must match expected fork version for the requested slot. Malformed responses must be rejected.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_ada88c29a21d2.target_component_interface: SSZ deserialization for light client messages
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_ada88c29a21d2.security_assumption: Fork version must be determined from slot/epoch before selecting SSZ type. Deserialization with wrong type must fail safely without crashes or memory corruption. Messages at genesis fork version must be rejected.

Checkpoint root and epoch must be validated against chain state. Node must verify it is within the weak subjectivity period. If outside WS period, node must halt and require operator intervention for fresh checkpoint.
Conflicting chains must be rejected if they disagree with a valid WS checkpoint within the WS period. Node must track WS period expiry and refuse to sync if exceeded.

Effective balances must be frozen at epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1 before RANDAO for epoch N is known. Proposer schedule stored in state must be immutable once computed. Lookahead vector must be initialized correctly at fork activation.

outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_ada88c29a21d2.target_component_interface: RANDAO seed retrieval for proposer computation
outputs/01b_SUBGRAPHS/spec_ada88c29a21d2.security_assumption: RANDAO values must be unpredictable at the time effective balances are set. MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD provides the temporal separation. If RANDAO prediction advances, the security margin must be re-evaluated.
